sentences.zh: 王世充王世充字行滿。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong — Wang Shichong, whose style was Xingman.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong — Wang Shichong, styled Xingman.

sentences.zh: 祖西域胡，號支頹耨，後徙新豐，死，其妻與霸城人王粲為庶妻。

translations.literal: His grandfather was a barbarian from the Western Regions, called Zhi Tuinao; later they moved to Xinfeng. When he died, his wife became a concubine of Wang Can of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was a man of western-region origin known as Zhi Tuinao; the family later moved to Xinfeng. After he died, his widow became a concubine of Wang Can of Baling.

sentences.zh: 頹耨子收從之子，冒粲姓，仕隋，歷懷、汴二州長史。

translations.literal: Tuinao's son Shou was a son born to a concubine; he took the surname Can, entered Sui service, and served in succession as chief administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Tuinao's son Shou was born to a concubine; he adopted the surname Can, entered Sui service, and served successively as chief administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 生世充，豺聲卷發，忌刻深阻。

translations.literal: He fathered Shichong, who had a jackal-like voice and curly hair, and was jealous, harsh, and deeply obstructive.
translations.idiomatic: He fathered Shichong, who spoke in a harsh, jackal-like voice, wore his hair in curls, and was jealous, spiteful, and treacherous by nature.

sentences.zh: 涉書傳，喜兵法，通龜策、推步。

translations.literal: He studied the classics and histories, delighted in military strategy, and was versed in tortoise-shell divination and calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in the classics and histories, took to military strategy, and mastered tortoise-shell divination and calendrical reckoning.

sentences.zh: 以廕為左翊衛，遷禦府直長、兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: By hereditary privilege he became a guard of the Left Flank, and was promoted to direct steward of the Imperial Storehouse and vice minister of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered service as a guard of the Left Flank, then rose to direct steward of the Imperial Storehouse and vice minister of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 從楊素北伐，為幽州長史。

translations.literal: He followed Yang Su on the northern campaign and served as chief administrator of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Yang Su on the northern campaign and served as chief administrator of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 大業初，為民部侍郎，善占對，習法，敢舞文上下。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Daye reign he became vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue; he was skilled at impromptu replies, versed in law, and dared to twist statutes to his advantage up and down.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue. He was quick with impromptu replies, well versed in law, and bold enough to bend statutes to serve his own ends.

sentences.zh: 人或辨駁，世充以口舌緣飾，眾知其非，亦不能屈也。

translations.literal: When others argued against him, Shichong would ornament his case with glib speech; the crowd knew he was wrong, yet could not refute him.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone challenged him, Shichong would paper over the flaws with slick rhetoric; people could see he was wrong, yet still could not bring him down in debate.

sentences.zh: 出為江都贊治，遷郡丞。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as assistant administrator of Jiangdu and was promoted to deputy prefect of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as assistant administrator of Jiangdu and later promoted to deputy prefect of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 煬帝數南幸，世充善伺帝顏色，阿意順旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang made many southern tours; Shichong was adept at watching the emperor's expression and currying favor by agreeing with his wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang often toured the south, and Shichong was expert at reading his mood and winning favor by echoing whatever the emperor wanted to hear.

sentences.zh: 性機巧，飾臺沼、陰奏遠方珍物以媚帝，帝愛昵之，拜江都通守，兼知宮監事。

translations.literal: By nature he was ingenious; he adorned terraces and ponds, secretly presented rare objects from distant regions to please the emperor, and the emperor grew fond of him, appointing him communications commissioner of Jiangdu while also putting him in charge of palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Clever by nature, he beautified terraces and ponds and quietly sent rare tribute from distant regions to court the emperor's favor. Yang grew attached to him, made him communications commissioner of Jiangdu, and put him in charge of palace affairs as well.

sentences.zh: 世充觀隋政方亂，而江左浮剽易動，乃陰結豪桀，有繫獄者，皆橈法貸減，以樹私恩。

translations.literal: Shichong saw that Sui government was falling into disorder and that the Jiangzuo region was frivolous, predatory, and easy to stir up; he therefore secretly joined with bold men, and for all who were imprisoned he bent the law to grant release or reduction of sentence, thereby building private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Sui rule was coming apart and that the lower Yangtze country was restless and easily roused, Shichong quietly allied himself with local strongmen; whenever anyone was in prison he would bend the law to secure release or lighter punishment and thereby build a private following.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感反，吳人硃燮、晉陵人管崇起江南應之，兵十余萬。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling rose in the south of the Yangtze to answer him, with an army of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinling raised forces south of the Yangtze in support, mustering more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 隋將吐萬緒、魚俱羅討之不克，世充以偏將募江都萬人，頻擊破之。

translations.literal: The Sui generals Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo campaigned against them without success; Shichong, as a subordinate commander, recruited ten thousand men from Jiangdu and repeatedly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Sui generals Tuwan Xu and Yu Juluo failed to suppress them, but Shichong, serving as a subordinate commander, raised ten thousand men from Jiangdu and repeatedly routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 每捷必歸功於下。

translations.literal: Whenever he won a victory he always attributed the merit to his subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: After every victory he always gave the credit to his men.

sentences.zh: 虜獲盡推與士卒，故人爭為效，由是功最多。

translations.literal: Captives and booty he entirely passed on to the soldiers, so men vied to serve him, and thus his achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: He turned over all captives and spoils to the troops, so men competed to fight under him, and in this way he won the most credit.

sentences.zh: 大業十年，齊賊孟讓轉寇諸郡，至盱眙，世充拒之，保都梁山，列五壁不戰，羸兵以示弱。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Daye, the Qi bandit Meng Rang raided through the commanderies and reached Xuyi; Shichong resisted him, defended the capital at Liangshan, set up five ramparts and would not give battle, and displayed weak troops to show feebleness.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Daye the Qi rebel Meng Rang swept through the commanderies as far as Xuyi. Shichong met him there, withdrew to defend Liangshan, built five walled camps, and refused battle, posting only weak-looking troops to feign weakness.

sentences.zh: 讓笑曰：「世充文法吏，安知兵？

translations.literal: Rang laughed and said, "Shichong is a clerk of statutes and regulations — how would he know warfare?
translations.idiomatic: Rang laughed and said, "Shichong is nothing but a legal clerk — what does he know of war?

sentences.zh: 吾今生縛之，鼓行下江都矣！」

translations.literal: I shall bind him alive today and march straight down to Jiangdu!
translations.idiomatic: I'll take him alive today and march straight on Jiangdu!

sentences.zh: 時百姓皆入保，野無所掠，讓眾餧，又苦五壁閉道不得南，即分兵圍之。

translations.literal: At that time the common people had all entered the fortified camps, and in the countryside there was nothing to plunder; Rang's host grew hungry, and they were further troubled because the five ramparts blocked the road and they could not advance south, so they divided their forces to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: By then the local population had all taken refuge in the camps, leaving nothing to plunder in the countryside. Rang's army went hungry, and the five ramparts blocked the road south, so they split their forces and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 世充數戰，陽不利，走壁；

translations.literal: Shichong fought several engagements, feigning defeat and retreating to the ramparts;
translations.idiomatic: Shichong fought several skirmishes, pretended to lose, and fell back into the ramparts;

sentences.zh: 讓益驕，數日，稍分其下南略，裁留兵足圍壁。

translations.literal: Rang grew still more arrogant; after several days he gradually sent part of his force south to raid, keeping only enough troops to besiege the ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Rang grew bolder still. After a few days he began sending detachments south to raid, leaving behind only enough men to keep the camps under siege.

sentences.zh: 世充知賊懈，夜夷竈撤幕，為方陣外向，毀垣而出，奮擊，大破之，讓以數十騎去，斬首萬級，虜十余萬人。

translations.literal: Shichong knew the bandits had slackened; at night he leveled the cooking pits, removed the tent screens, formed square arrays facing outward, broke through the walls and sallied forth, struck fiercely, and routed them utterly. Rang fled with several dozen horsemen; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and captives exceeded a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong saw the enemy had grown careless, he struck at night: cooking pits were cleared away, tent screens removed, and his men formed outward-facing squares, broke through the walls, and charged. The rebels were shattered. Rang escaped with only a few dozen horsemen; more than ten thousand heads were taken and captives numbered over a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以世充有將帥略，復委捕諸盜，所向輒定。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, because Shichong had the capacity of a commander, again entrusted him with suppressing the various bandits; wherever he went, order was quickly restored.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that Shichong had real commander's talent, Emperor Yang again put him in charge of hunting down the bandits, and wherever he went the situation was quickly brought under control.

sentences.zh: 會突厥圍帝雁門，世充悉發江都兵赴難，詐為可喜事以邀聲譽。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen, Shichong mobilized all the Jiangdu troops to the rescue and feigned acceptable conduct to win reputation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen, Shichong marched out with every soldier he could raise from Jiangdu and staged acts of loyal devotion to win acclaim.

sentences.zh: 在軍蓬首垢面，日夜悲泣，不釋甲，臥必席槁。

translations.literal: In camp he went with disheveled hair and a filthy face, weeping day and night, never removing his armor, and when he lay down he always slept on straw matting.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he let his hair hang unkempt and his face go unwashed, wept day and night, never took off his armor, and slept only on a bed of straw.

sentences.zh: 帝以為忠，愈屬信之。

translations.literal: The emperor took this for loyalty and trusted him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this as proof of loyalty and relied on him ever more heavily.

sentences.zh: 厭次賊格謙兵十余萬屯豆子，太仆卿楊義臣殺謙，世充討其余黨，夷之。

translations.literal: The Yanci bandit Ge Qian, with an army of more than a hundred thousand, encamped at Douzi; the grand master of the imperial stud Yang Yichen killed Qian, and Shichong campaigned against the remaining factions and exterminated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yanci rebel Ge Qian held more than a hundred thousand men at Douzi. Grand Master of the Imperial Stud Yang Yichen killed Qian, and Shichong then hunted down the remaining bands and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 進擊賊盧明月於南陽，俘系數萬。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack the bandit Lu Mingyue at Nanyang and captured and bound several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the rebel Lu Mingyue at Nanyang and took tens of thousands prisoner.

sentences.zh: 還，帝自持酒為勞。

translations.literal: On his return the emperor personally brought wine to reward him.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, the emperor himself brought wine to toast his service.

sentences.zh: 世充啟帝：「江淮良家女願備後廷，無繇進。」

translations.literal: Shichong reported to the emperor: "Good families of the Jianghuai region wish to enter the rear apartments but have no means of doing so.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong told the emperor, "Women of respectable families in the Jianghuai region wish to enter the inner palace but have no way to present themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，令閱端麗者，以庫貲為聘，費不可校，署計簿雲「敕別用」，有司不敢聞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and ordered a review of the most comely; betrothal gifts were paid from the treasury stores, the expense beyond reckoning, and the account books were marked "by special imperial order" — the responsible offices dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and ordered the most beautiful selected. Betrothal payments came from the treasury at a cost beyond counting; the ledgers were marked "for separate imperial use," and the responsible offices dared not report the expense.

sentences.zh: 具舟送東都宮，會道路剽奪，使者苦之，或沈舟亡去，世充屏不奏。

translations.literal: Boats were prepared to send them to the Eastern Capital palace; but on the roads there was plundering, and the envoys suffered; some sank their boats and fled, and Shichong suppressed the reports and did not memorialize them.
translations.idiomatic: He fitted out boats to send the women to the palace at the Eastern Capital, but banditry along the route made the mission miserable; some envoys scuttled their boats and fled. Shichong hushed it up and never reported the losses.

sentences.zh: 李密逼東都，詔世充為將軍，以兵屯洛口。

translations.literal: When Li Mi pressed the Eastern Capital, an edict made Shichong a general and stationed his troops at Luokou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi threatened the Eastern Capital, an edict appointed Shichong general and posted his army at Luokou.

sentences.zh: 大小百余戰，無大勝負。

translations.literal: They fought more than a hundred engagements large and small, with no great victory or defeat on either side.
translations.idiomatic: They fought more than a hundred clashes, large and small, without a decisive outcome on either side.

sentences.zh: 詔即拜右翊衛將軍，趣破賊。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed him general of the Right Flank Guard and urged him to destroy the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promptly appointed general of the Right Flank Guard with orders to crush the rebels at once.

sentences.zh: 十四年，世充引軍與密戰洛南，有氣若城壓其營，世充大敗，眾幾盡，走保河陽。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he led his army to fight Mi south of the Luo; a vapor like a city wall pressed down on his camp, and Shichong was utterly defeated, his force nearly annihilated; he fled to defend Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he brought his army against Mi south of the Luo River. A mass of vapor like a city wall seemed to press down on his camp; Shichong was routed, his force nearly wiped out, and he fled to hold Heyang.

sentences.zh: 自繫獄，請罪於越王侗，侗以書慰勉，賜金帛安之，召還洛，裒亡散得萬人，屯含嘉城，畏縮不敢出。

translations.literal: He bound himself and entered prison, begging punishment from Yang Tong, Prince of Yue; Tong sent a letter to comfort and encourage him, bestowed gold and silk to reassure him, summoned him back to Luoyang, gathered the scattered dead and survivors to ten thousand men, encamped at Hanjia Fortress, and shrank back in fear, not daring to sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: He put himself in chains and begged punishment from Yang Tong, Prince of Yue. Tong wrote to comfort him, sent gold and silk to reassure him, and recalled him to Luoyang. Shichong gathered the scattered remnants to ten thousand men, encamped at Hanjia Fortress, and was too afraid to venture out again.

sentences.zh: 會江都殺逆，群臣奉侗為帝，以世充為吏部尚書，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: When the regicide at Jiangdu occurred, the ministers enthroned Tong as emperor, made Shichong minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the assassination at Jiangdu took place, the court ministers enthroned Tong as emperor, appointed Shichong minister of the Ministry of Personnel, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及擁兵北還，侗聽內史令元文都、盧楚等謀，以重官畀李密，使討賊，若化及破而密兵亦疲，乘其弊，可得誌。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji led his army back north; Tong followed the counsel of the chief secretariat Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and others: bestow high office on Li Mi and send him to attack the rebel; if Huaji were broken and Mi's troops also worn down, they could seize the moment of weakness and achieve their aim.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji was marching north with his army. Tong accepted a plan from Chief Secretariat Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, and others: offer Li Mi high office and send him against Huaji; once Huaji was broken and Mi's forces exhausted as well, they could strike at the weakened victor and achieve their goal.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使以太尉、尚書令即軍中拜密，趣兵北討。

translations.literal: They therefore sent envoys to invest Mi in camp as Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and urge his army north to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys were sent to invest Mi in the field as Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat and to hurry his army north against Huaji.

sentences.zh: 密稱臣奉制，引後從化及黎陽，戰勝來告，眾大悅；

translations.literal: Mi styled himself a subject obeying the imperial command, followed after Huaji to Liyang, reported victory in battle, and the court was greatly pleased;
translations.idiomatic: Mi declared himself the emperor's loyal subject, pursued Huaji to Liyang, reported a victory, and the court rejoiced;

sentences.zh: 世充獨謂其下曰：「文都等刀筆才，必為密禽，且我軍與賊戰，多殺其父子兄弟，一旦為之下，吾屬無類矣！」

translations.literal: Shichong alone told his followers: "Wendu and the rest are mere pen-and-ink men — they are sure to be captured by Mi; moreover our army has fought the bandits and killed many of their fathers, sons, and brothers. Once we are placed under them, none of us will survive!
translations.idiomatic: Shichong alone told his men, "Wendu and his crowd are mere clerks — Mi is bound to swallow them. And our army has killed too many of Mi's kin in battle. If we ever fall under his command, none of us will be left alive!

sentences.zh: 以此言激眾，文都等聞，大懼。

translations.literal: With these words he stirred the troops; when Wendu and the others heard of it they were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: With these words he stirred up his troops. When Wendu and the others heard of it they were terrified.

sentences.zh: 侗欲以文都為御史大夫，世充不許，曰：「嘗與公等約，左右仆射、尚書令、御史大夫，留待勛舊。

translations.literal: Tong wished to make Wendu censor-in-chief; Shichong would not allow it and said, "We once agreed among ourselves that the posts of left and right vice premier, director of the secretariat, and censor-in-chief would be reserved for men of merit and long service.
translations.idiomatic: Tong wanted to make Wendu censor-in-chief, but Shichong refused, saying, "We agreed among ourselves that the vice premierships, the directorship of the secretariat, and the censorate would be reserved for men of merit and long service.

sentences.zh: 今各欲得，則流競開矣，何以共守？」

translations.literal: Now if each wants to seize them, factional strife will open up — how can we hold together in defense?
translations.idiomatic: If everyone grabs for them now, factional strife will break out. How can we hold the city together?

sentences.zh: 文都憾焉，潛與楚謀，因世充入殿伏甲殺之。

translations.literal: Wendu resented this and secretly plotted with Chu to set armed men in ambush when Shichong entered the hall and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu took this as a grievous insult and secretly plotted with Chu to ambush Shichong with hidden troops when he next entered the hall.

sentences.zh: 納言段達庸怯，畏不果，馳告世充。

translations.literal: The palace counselor Duan Da was mediocre and timid; in fear he did not carry it out and galloped to inform Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Counselor Duan Da was timid and weak-willed; afraid to act, he galloped off to warn Shichong instead.

sentences.zh: 世充夜以兵襲含嘉門，圍宮城。

translations.literal: Shichong by night led troops in a surprise attack on the Hanjia Gate and besieged the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shichong struck at the Hanjia Gate with his troops and besieged the palace city.

sentences.zh: 右武衛大將軍皇甫無逸等遣將費曜、田阇拒戰太陽門，曜敗，世充入之，無逸以單騎遁，收楚殺之。

translations.literal: The general of the Right Martial Guard Huangfu Wuyi and others sent the commanders Fei Yao and Tian She to resist at the Taiyang Gate; Yao was defeated, Shichong entered, Wuyi fled alone on horseback, and Chu was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: General of the Right Martial Guard Huangfu Wuyi sent Fei Yao and Tian She to hold the Taiyang Gate. Yao was beaten, Shichong broke through, Wuyi fled alone on horseback, and Chu was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 時紫微宮尚閉世充扣門，紿侗曰：「元文都等欲執陛下降李密，臣不反，誅反者耳。」

translations.literal: At that time the Ziwei Palace was still closed; Shichong knocked at the gate and deceived Tong, saying, "Yuan Wendu and the rest wished to seize Your Majesty and surrender you to Li Mi — I have not rebelled; I have only executed rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Ziwei Palace gates were still shut when Shichong knocked and lied to Tong: "Yuan Wendu and his faction meant to seize Your Majesty and hand you over to Li Mi. I have not rebelled — I have only killed rebels.

sentences.zh: 段達執文都送世充，殺之。

translations.literal: Duan Da seized Wendu and handed him to Shichong, who killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da seized Wendu and delivered him to Shichong, who had him killed.

sentences.zh: 世充悉遣腹心代衛士，然後入謝曰：「文都、楚無狀，規相屠戮，臣急為此，非敢它。」

translations.literal: Shichong sent all his trusted men to replace the palace guards, then entered to apologize and said, "Wendu and Chu were lawless and plotted mutual slaughter; I acted in haste for this reason and dared do nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong replaced the palace guards with his own trusted men, then went in to apologize: "Wendu and Chu were out of control and meant to butcher one another. I acted in haste — I had no other design.

sentences.zh: 侗與之盟，進拜尚書左仆射，總督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Tong made a covenant with him, promoted him to left vice premier of the secretariat, and put him in overall command of all military affairs within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Tong swore an alliance with him, promoted him to left vice premier of the secretariat, and gave him overall command of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 乃去含嘉城，居尚書省，專宰朝政，以其兄世惲為內史令，居禁中，子弟皆將兵。

translations.literal: He then left Hanjia Fortress, took up residence in the Secretariat, and monopolized court government; he made his elder brother Shiyun chief secretariat and stationed him in the forbidden quarters, while his sons and younger brothers all held military commands.
translations.idiomatic: He moved out of Hanjia Fortress into the Secretariat and took sole control of government. His elder brother Shiyun became chief secretariat and lived inside the palace; his sons and younger brothers all held military commands.

sentences.zh: 分官吏為十頭，以主軍政。

translations.literal: He divided officials into ten heads to administer military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the bureaucracy into ten sections, each in charge of military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密破化及，還屯金墉，勁兵良馬多死。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji, returned to encamp at Jinyong, and many of his crack troops and fine horses had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji and withdrew to camp at Jinyong, but many of his best soldiers and horses had been lost in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 世充欲擊之，恐士心未一，乃謀以鬼動眾，令德陽門衛張永通言夢人謂己曰：「我，周公，能以兵助討密。」

translations.literal: Shichong wished to attack him but feared the troops were not of one mind; he therefore plotted to move the host by spirits, and had the Deyang Gate guard Zhang Yongtong say that in a dream a man told him: "I am the Duke of Zhou — I can aid you with troops to attack Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wanted to strike but feared his men were not united. He therefore staged a supernatural sign, having Deyang Gate guard Zhang Yongtong report a dream in which a man said, "I am the Duke of Zhou — I can lend you troops to attack Mi.

sentences.zh: 世充白侗，立祠洛旁，使巫宣言：「周公令急擊密，有大功；

translations.literal: Shichong reported this to Tong, erected a shrine beside the Luo, and had shamans proclaim: "The Duke of Zhou orders a swift attack on Mi — great merit awaits;
translations.idiomatic: Shichong reported this to Tong, built a shrine by the Luo, and had shamans announce, "The Duke of Zhou commands a swift attack on Mi — great reward awaits;

sentences.zh: 不然，兵且疫。」

translations.literal: otherwise the army will suffer pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: otherwise the army will be struck by plague.

sentences.zh: 世充下皆楚人，信妖，遂請戰。

translations.literal: All of Shichong's subordinates were men of Chu and believed in the supernatural; they therefore asked for battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's followers were mostly men of Chu and believers in omens, so they pressed for battle.

sentences.zh: 乃簡精卒二萬、騎二千，跨洛水為三橋以度兵。

translations.literal: He then selected twenty thousand elite infantry and two thousand horsemen, and threw three bridges across the Luo to move his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He picked twenty thousand elite foot soldiers and two thousand cavalry, then threw three bridges across the Luo to move his army across.

sentences.zh: 密軍偃師北山，新破敵，有輕世充心，不設壁壘。

translations.literal: Mi's army was on the northern hills of Yanshi; freshly victorious over the enemy, they held Shichong in contempt and did not set up ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's army camped on the northern hills of Yanshi. Fresh from victory, they despised Shichong and set up no fortifications.

sentences.zh: 世充夜遣二百騎蔽山伏，因秣馬蓐食，遲明薄之，密陣未成，伏兵上北原，乘高馳下，壓其營，縱焚廬落，密眾大潰，降其將張童仁、陳智略，進拔偃師。

translations.literal: Shichong by night sent two hundred horsemen to lie in ambush behind the hills; they fed their horses and took a bedside meal, and at the late dawn pressed the attack. Mi's battle line was not yet formed; the ambush climbed the northern plateau, charged down from the heights, bore down on his camp, and set fire to the huts. Mi's host was utterly routed; his generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue surrendered, and Shichong advanced to take Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: That night Shichong sent two hundred horsemen to hide behind the hills. After feeding their horses and taking a quick meal, they struck at first light before Mi's line was formed. The ambush swept down from the northern heights, overran the camp, and set the shelters ablaze. Mi's army collapsed. Generals Zhang Tongren and Chen Zhilue surrendered, and Shichong took Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 初，密得世充兄世偉及子玄應於化及軍，囚之，至是皆歸。

translations.literal: Earlier Mi had captured Shichong's elder brother Shiwei and his son Xuanying from Huaji's army and imprisoned them; now they were all returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mi had taken Shichong's brother Shiwei and his son Xuanying from Huaji's army and held them prisoner; now both were returned.

sentences.zh: 世充兵次洛口，密長史邴元真、司馬鄭虔象以城降，悉收美人、寶貨而還。

translations.literal: Shichong's army halted at Luokou; Mi's chief administrator Bing Yuanzhen and marshal Zheng Qianxiang surrendered the city; he gathered all the beautiful women and precious goods and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's army reached Luokou. Mi's chief administrator Bing Yuanzhen and marshal Zheng Qianxiang surrendered the city. Shichong seized the women and treasure and marched back.

sentences.zh: 密以數十騎跳奔。

translations.literal: Mi fled on horseback with several dozen riders.
translations.idiomatic: Mi escaped with only a few dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 於是，世充自為太尉、尚書令，加黃門印綠綟綬，以尚書省為府，置官屬。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shichong made himself Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, added the yellow-gate seal and green ribbon, made the Secretariat his headquarters, and established a staff of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shichong made himself Grand Marshal and Director of the Imperial Secretariat, took the yellow-gate seal and green ribbon of rank, turned the Secretariat into his headquarters, and set up a full staff of officials.

sentences.zh: 乃設三榜於府外，其一求文學堪濟世務者，其一武幹絕眾、推鋒陷陣者，其一能治冤抑不申者。

translations.literal: He then set up three public notices outside his headquarters: one sought men of literary learning fit to manage affairs of state; one sought martial talent surpassing the multitude, able to drive the van and break enemy lines; one sought men able to redress wrongs suppressed without redress.
translations.idiomatic: He posted three public notices outside his headquarters: one called for scholars capable of governing; one for warriors of exceptional skill who could lead charges and break enemy lines; one for men able to right grievances that had gone unheard.

sentences.zh: 繇是上書陳事日數百，皆慰勞省接，雖吏卒，必飾詞誘納。

translations.literal: From this, memorials stating affairs numbered in the hundreds each day; he comforted and received them all, and even clerks and soldiers he would always adorn his words to entice and win over.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of petitions arrived each day, and he received them all with courtesy and encouragement. Even common clerks and soldiers he would flatter and win over with fine words.

sentences.zh: 而世充素詭妄，不能仇其語，士大夫遂貳。

translations.literal: Yet Shichong had always been deceitful and false and could not live up to his words, and the scholar-officials therefore became divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: But Shichong had always been deceitful and could not keep his promises, so the gentry and officials began to turn away from him.

sentences.zh: 初，殺文都，欲詭眾取信，乃請事侗母劉太后為假子，至是加號聖感太后。

translations.literal: Earlier, after killing Wendu, wishing to deceive the masses and win trust, he had asked to serve Tong's mother, Empress Dowager Liu, as a foster son; now he added for her the title Sagely Responsive Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: After killing Wendu he had asked to become foster son to Tong's mother, Empress Dowager Liu, in order to win public trust; now he gave her the additional title Sagely Responsive Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍崔德本曰：「此王莽文母何異乎？」

translations.literal: The attendant gentleman Cui Deben said, "How is this different from Wang Mang's Wenmu?
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Gentleman Cui Deben remarked, "How is this any different from Wang Mang and his 'Wenmu'?

sentences.zh: 後食侗前，得嘔疾，疑見毒，遂不復朝。

translations.literal: Later, when he ate before Tong, he suffered vomiting and suspected he had been poisoned; he therefore no longer attended court.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he dined in Tong's presence he was seized with vomiting, suspected poison, and never attended court again.

sentences.zh: 以將張績、董浚衛宮城。

translations.literal: He placed the generals Zhang Ji and Dong Jun to guard the palace city.
translations.idiomatic: He posted generals Zhang Ji and Dong Jun to guard the palace city.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，矯侗詔假黃鉞，相國總百揆，封鄭王，授九錫，冕十有二旒，建天子旌旗，金根車，駕六馬，備五時副車、旄頭雲罕，舞八佾，設宮縣，出入警蹕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude, by a forged edict of Tong he was lent the yellow battle-axe, made chief minister with authority over all affairs, enfeoffed as King of Zheng, granted the Nine Bestowals, a cap with twelve tassels, imperial banners, the golden-root carriage, six-horse teams, the five seasonal secondary carriages, maotou and yunhan standards, eight rows of dancers, palace music, and imperial escort on going out and coming in.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wude a forged edict from Tong lent him the yellow battle-axe, made him chief minister with authority over all government, enfeoffed him as King of Zheng, and granted the Nine Bestowals: a twelve-tassel crown, imperial banners, the golden-root carriage, six-horse teams, the five seasonal secondary carriages, maotou and yunhan standards, eight rows of dancers, palace music, and imperial escort whenever he went abroad.

sentences.zh: 術士桓法嗣自言能決讖，乃上《孔子閉房記》，畫男子持一竿驅羊狀，因說世充曰：「隋，楊姓也；

translations.literal: The adept Huan Fasi claimed he could interpret prophetic texts and presented the «Record of Confucius Secluding Himself in a Chamber», with a picture of a man holding a pole driving sheep; he then explained to Shichong: 「Sui is the surname Yang;
translations.idiomatic: The occultist Huan Fasi claimed he could interpret prophetic texts and presented the «Record of Confucius Secluding Himself in a Chamber», illustrated with a man holding a pole and driving sheep. He told Shichong, 「Sui is the Yang clan;

sentences.zh: 於文，『幹一』為『王』，王處羊後，大王代隋之符。」

translations.literal: in writing, 'gan-yi' forms 'wang'; the king stands after the sheep — this is the token that the Great King will replace Sui."
translations.idiomatic: in writing, 'gan' plus 'yi' makes 'wang'; the king comes after the sheep — the sign that Your Greatness will replace the Sui."

sentences.zh: 又陳莊周《人間世》、《德充符》二篇曰：「上下篇與大王名協，明受符命，德被人間，為天子也。」

translations.literal: He also cited Zhuangzi's «In the Human World» and «Sign of the Fulfilled Virtue» and said: 「The upper and lower chapters accord with the Great King's name — clearly he has received the mandate, his virtue fills the human world, and he is to be Son of Heaven.」
translations.idiomatic: He also cited Zhuangzi's «In the Human World» and «Sign of the Fulfilled Virtue», saying, 「The titles of these two chapters match Your Greatness's name — a clear sign that you have received Heaven's mandate, your virtue fills the world, and you are destined to be Son of Heaven.」

sentences.zh: 世充喜曰：「天命也！」

translations.literal: Shichong rejoiced and said, "Heaven's mandate!"
translations.idiomatic: Shichong exclaimed with delight, "It is Heaven's mandate!"

sentences.zh: 拜受之。

translations.literal: He bowed and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and accepted the interpretation.

sentences.zh: 以法嗣為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He made Fasi a remonstrance counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Fasi remonstrance counselor.

sentences.zh: 又羅取飛鳥，書符命於帛，系鳥頸縱之，有彈捕得鳥而獻者亦拜官。

translations.literal: He also netted birds, wrote the mandate of fate on silk, tied it to their necks and released them; those who shot down a bird with a pellet-bow and presented it were also given office.
translations.idiomatic: He also caught birds, wrote prophetic messages on silk, tied them to the birds' necks, and released them. Anyone who shot down such a bird with a pellet bow and presented it was also given an official post.

sentences.zh: 諷百官勸進。

translations.literal: He prompted the hundred officials to urge his advance to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He prompted the officials to urge him to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 時納言蘇威老就第，世充以威隋大臣，有素望，每表必署威名。

translations.literal: At that time the palace counselor Su Wei was old and retired to his estate; Shichong, because Wei was an elder minister of Sui with long-standing reputation, always signed Wei's name on every memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Counselor Su Wei was by then old and living in retirement. Because Wei was a senior Sui minister of long-standing reputation, Shichong signed Wei's name on every memorial.

sentences.zh: 使段達等脅侗曰：「天命不常，今鄭王功德甚盛，請揖讓，用堯、舜故事。」

translations.literal: He had Duan Da and others coerce Tong, saying, "Heaven's mandate is not constant; now the King of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great — we beg abdication in the manner of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: He had Duan Da and others pressure Tong: "Heaven's mandate does not rest on one house forever. The King of Zheng's merit is now overwhelming — we beg Your Majesty to yield the throne in the manner of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 侗怒曰：「天下者，高祖天下，若隋德未究，此言不可發。

translations.literal: Tong angrily said, "The realm is the realm of the High Ancestor; if Sui virtue is not yet exhausted, such words must not be spoken.
translations.idiomatic: Tong burst out in anger: "This realm belongs to the High Ancestor. If Sui virtue is not yet spent, such talk must not be uttered.

sentences.zh: 必天命遂改，尚何禪？

translations.literal: If Heaven's mandate has truly changed, what need is there for abdication?
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven's mandate has truly changed, what need is there for a ceremonial abdication?

sentences.zh: 公非先帝舊臣乎？

translations.literal: Are you not an old servant of the late emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Were you not a loyal servant of the late emperor?

sentences.zh: 朕何賴？」

translations.literal: On whom can I rely?"
translations.idiomatic: On whom can I possibly rely?"

sentences.zh: 達等流涕。

translations.literal: Duan and the others wept.
translations.idiomatic: Duan and the others burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 世充又詐曰：「天下未定，須鎮以長君，待天下安，則復子明辟。」

translations.literal: Shichong again deceived him, saying, "The realm is not yet settled; we must steady it with a mature ruler; when the realm is at peace, I shall restore the son to clear rule."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong lied again: "The realm is still unsettled. We need a seasoned ruler to hold it steady. When peace returns, I shall restore Your Majesty to open rule."

sentences.zh: 四月，矯侗策禪位，幽侗於含涼殿，猶三讓。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, by a forged edict of Tong the abdication was enacted; Tong was confined in the Hall of Gentle Coolness, and Shichong still performed the three refusals.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month a forged edict from Tong enacted the abdication. Tong was confined in the Hall of Gentle Coolness while Shichong still went through the ritual three refusals.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將以兵清宮，世充襲戎服，法駕，導鼓吹入宮，每歷一門，從者必呼。

translations.literal: He sent the generals with troops to clear the palace; Shichong donned military dress, took the imperial equipage, and entered the palace with guiding music and drums; at every gate he passed, his followers had to shout.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals with troops to clear the palace. Shichong put on military dress, took the imperial procession, and entered to the sound of drums and pipes. At every gate his followers shouted.

sentences.zh: 至東上閤，更兗冕，即正殿僭位。

translations.literal: At the eastern upper pavilion he changed into the imperial cap and robes and usurped the throne in the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the eastern upper pavilion he changed into imperial regalia and took the throne in the main hall.

sentences.zh: 建元開明，國號鄭。

translations.literal: He established the era name Kaiming and the state name Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the era name Kaiming and adopted Zheng as the name of his state.

sentences.zh: 乃封兄世衡為秦王，世偉楚王，世惲齊王，諸族屬以次封拜，以子玄應為皇太子，玄恕為漢王。

translations.literal: He then enfeoffed his elder brother Shiheng as King of Qin, Shiwei as King of Chu, Shiyun as King of Qi, and enfeoffed the clansmen in order; he made his son Xuanying crown prince and Xuanxu King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his elder brother Shiheng as King of Qin, Shiwei as King of Chu, and Shiyun as King of Qi, while other kinsmen received titles in turn. His son Xuanying became crown prince and Xuanxu was made King of Han.

sentences.zh: 世充每聽朝決政，誨喻言語諄復百緒，以示勤篤，百司奏事者聽受為疲。

translations.literal: Whenever Shichong held court to decide affairs of government, his admonitions and instructions were repetitiously elaborated on countless topics, to display diligence and sincerity, and officials who came to report business grew weary of listening.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wang Shichong held court to decide policy, he lectured at tedious length on every conceivable subject to show how diligent and devoted he was, until officials reporting business were worn out from listening.

sentences.zh: 出則輕騎，無警蹕，遊歷衢肆，行者但止立，徐謂百姓曰：「故時天子居九重，在下之情無繇察。

translations.literal: When he went out he rode with a light escort, without imperial guards clearing the road; he toured the market streets, and passersby need only stop and stand aside as he slowly told the common people: "In former times the Son of Heaven dwelt within the ninefold palaces, and the feelings of those below had no means of being observed.
translations.idiomatic: When he went abroad he traveled with a light escort and no road-clearing guard; he wandered through the market streets, and travelers had only to stop and stand aside while he slowly told the people: "In the old days the emperor lived shut away in the inner palace, and the feelings of those below could not be seen.

sentences.zh: 世充非貪位者，本救時耳。

translations.literal: Shichong is not one who covets the throne; he seeks only to save the age.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong is not greedy for the throne; he seeks only to rescue the times.

sentences.zh: 正若一州刺史，事皆親覽，當與士人共議之。

translations.literal: Just as a prefect of a single province personally examines every matter, he ought to deliberate on them together with scholars and officials.
translations.idiomatic: Just as a provincial governor personally reviews every matter, he should discuss affairs together with the gentry and officials.

sentences.zh: 恐門衛有禁，無以盡通，今止順天門外置座聽事。」

translations.literal: For fear that gate guards might impose restrictions and prevent full access, he now simply sets out a seat outside the Shuntian Gate to hear petitions.
translations.idiomatic: He feared that palace gate guards would block access and keep people from reaching him, so he now simply placed a seat outside the Shuntian Gate to hear petitions.

sentences.zh: 又詔西朝堂聽冤訴，東朝堂延諫者。

translations.literal: He also decreed that the western audience hall would hear complaints of injustice, and the eastern audience hall would receive those who came to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered that the western audience hall hear grievances of injustice and the eastern audience hall receive those who came to offer remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 繇是章牘真委，觀省不暇，後亦不能復出。

translations.literal: From this, petitions and memorials piled up in truth and detail; he had no time even to look them over, and afterward he could no longer go out either.
translations.idiomatic: From then on petitions and memorials poured in in such volume that he had no time to review them, and afterward he could no longer go out at all.

sentences.zh: 五月，裴仁基與其子行儼及宇文儒童、崔德本等謀劫世充，復立侗，不克，夷三族。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Pei Renji together with his son Xingyan and Yuwen Rutong, Cui Deben, and others plotted to seize Shichong and restore Yang Tong to the throne; they failed, and all three clans were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Pei Renji, his son Xingyan, Yuwen Rutong, Cui Deben, and others plotted to seize Wang Shichong and restore Yang Tong; the plot failed, and all three of their clans were exterminated.

sentences.zh: 六月，鴆殺侗，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Yang Tong was killed with poisoned wine, to cut off the hope of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Yang Tong was poisoned to death, so as to extinguish the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 世充率眾東徇地至滑，以兵臨黎陽。

translations.literal: Shichong led his army eastward to seize territory as far as Hua, and sent troops against Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong led his forces east to seize territory as far as Hua and sent troops against Liyang.

sentences.zh: 時黎陽為竇建德守，故建德亦破世充殷州，以報其役。

translations.literal: At that time Liyang was held by Dou Jiande, so Jiande also attacked Shichong's Yinzhou, in reprisal for this campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang was then held by Dou Jiande, so Jiande in turn attacked Wang Shichong's Yin Prefecture in retaliation for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，下書大赦，築練兵臺於伊闕。

translations.literal: In the third year of his reign, he issued an edict granting a general amnesty and built a drill platform at Yique.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of his reign he issued a general amnesty and built a drill platform at Yique.

sentences.zh: 守將羅士信、豆盧達稍稍歸國，世充顧下多背己，乃峻誅暴禁以威之。

translations.literal: The defending generals Luo Shixin and Dou Ludu gradually surrendered to the Tang, and Shichong, seeing that many under him were turning against him, imposed severe punishments and harsh prohibitions to intimidate them.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison generals Luo Shixin and Dou Ludu gradually defected to Tang, and Shichong, seeing that many of his subordinates were abandoning him, imposed harsh punishments and brutal prohibitions to intimidate them.

sentences.zh: 戶一人逃，家無少長皆坐，父子、兄弟、夫婦許相告免。

translations.literal: If one person from a household fled, every member of the family, young and old alike, was punished; fathers and sons, brothers, and husbands and wives were permitted to inform on one another to escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If one member of a household fled, every person in the family, young or old, was punished; fathers and sons, brothers, and husbands and wives were allowed to inform on one another to escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 令伍伍相保，一家叛，舉伍誅。

translations.literal: He ordered households to be grouped in mutual guaranties of five; if one household rebelled, the entire group of five was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He required households to be grouped in mutual guaranties of five; if one household rebelled, all five households in the group were executed.

sentences.zh: 樵牧出入皆為限，公私不聊生。

translations.literal: Gathering firewood and tending herds were both restricted, and neither public nor private life was tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: Even gathering firewood and tending livestock were restricted, and neither public nor private life was bearable.

sentences.zh: 遣臺省官督十二郡營田，行者自謂仙去。

translations.literal: He dispatched central government officials to supervise field-reclamation work in the twelve commanderies; those sent out jokingly said they were going off to become immortals.
translations.idiomatic: He sent central government officials to supervise field reclamation in the twelve commanderies, and those sent out joked that they were departing to become immortals.

sentences.zh: 以宮城為大獄，意所猜惡，必收系其人，內家屬宮中。

translations.literal: He turned the palace city into a great prison; anyone he suspected or hated was sure to be arrested and imprisoned, with his family members confined within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He turned the palace city into a great prison; anyone he suspected or hated was arrested and imprisoned, and their families were confined inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 或命將，亦質其孥乃遣。

translations.literal: When he ordered a general to take the field, he also held the general's wife and children as hostages before dispatching him.
translations.idiomatic: When he ordered a general to take the field, he also held the general's wife and children as hostages before sending him out.

sentences.zh: 既而囚質且萬口，食不足，餓死者日數十。

translations.literal: Before long prisoners and hostages numbered nearly ten thousand mouths; food was insufficient, and dozens died of starvation each day.
translations.idiomatic: Before long prisoners and hostages numbered nearly ten thousand mouths; food was insufficient, and dozens died of starvation every day.

sentences.zh: 七月，高祖詔秦王率兵攻之，至新安，屯保多下，敗世充於慈澗城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to lead troops against him; reaching Xin'an, many fortified camps submitted, and he defeated Shichong at Cijian Fort.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Emperor Gaozu ordered the Prince of Qin to lead troops against him; reaching Xin'an, many fortified camps surrendered, and he defeated Wang Shichong at Cijian Fort.

sentences.zh: 八月，王陳兵青城宮，世充悉精兵來拒，隔澗言曰：「隋失其國，天下分崩，長安、洛陽各有分地，吾常自守，不敢西顧。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the Prince arrayed his troops at Qingcheng Palace; Shichong mobilized all his elite forces to resist, and called across the stream: "The Sui lost its state and the realm split apart; Chang'an and Luoyang each held their allotted territory. I have always kept to my own domain and dared not look westward.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the Prince of Qin deployed his army at Qingcheng Palace; Wang Shichong mustered all his elite troops to resist and shouted across the stream: "The Sui lost its realm and the empire split apart; Chang'an and Luoyang each held its own territory. I have always kept to my own domain and dared not look westward.

sentences.zh: 熊、谷二州在度內，不取，敦鄰好也。

translations.literal: I did not seize the two prefectures of Xiong and Gu within my borders, cultivating neighborly goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: I did not take the two prefectures of Xiong and Gu within my borders, out of respect for neighborly goodwill.

sentences.zh: 今王遠涉吾地，越三崤，饋糧千里，勤師遠出，將何求？」

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has come far into my territory, crossed the Three Xiao passes, and supplies food from a thousand li away — what do you seek by toiling your army on so distant a campaign?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Highness has marched deep into my territory, crossed the Three Xiao passes, and supplies your army from a thousand li away — what do you seek by sending your troops so far on such a toilsome campaign?

sentences.zh: 王曰：「四海之人皆承唐正朔，獨公迷不復。

translations.literal: The Prince said: "All people under heaven now observe the Tang calendar; you alone persist in your delusion and will not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince replied: "All people under heaven now follow the Tang calendar; you alone persist in your delusion and refuse to submit.

sentences.zh: 東都士民來請師，陛下重違，我是以來。

translations.literal: The people of the Eastern Capital pleaded for an army; the Emperor could not lightly refuse them — that is why I have come.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the Eastern Capital pleaded for an army, and the Emperor could not lightly refuse them — that is why I have come.

sentences.zh: 公若降，富貴可保；

translations.literal: If you submit, wealth and honor can be preserved;
translations.idiomatic: If you submit, wealth and honor can be preserved;

sentences.zh: 必拒我，勉之，無多言！」

translations.literal: If you must resist me, then exert yourself — no more words!
translations.idiomatic: If you insist on resisting me, then do your best — no more words!

sentences.zh: 世充約割地，不許。

translations.literal: Shichong proposed ceding territory; this was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong proposed ceding territory, but the offer was rejected.

sentences.zh: 潁州總管田瓚請舉山南二十五郡歸。

translations.literal: Yingzhou regional inspector Tian Zan asked to surrender the twenty-five commanderies south of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhou regional inspector Tian Zan offered to surrender the twenty-five commanderies south of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 九月，王君廓進拔軒轅，徇地至管城，河南州縣以次降定。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Wang Junkuo advanced and captured Xuanyuan, swept territory as far as Guancheng, and the prefectures and counties of Henan submitted one after another.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Wang Junkuo advanced and captured Xuanyuan, swept territory as far as Guancheng, and the prefectures and counties of Henan surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 始竇建德與世充隙，至是建德遣使結好，並陳赴援意。

translations.literal: At first Dou Jiande and Shichong had been at odds, but now Jiande sent envoys to forge an alliance and stated his intention to come to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande and Wang Shichong had been at odds at first, but now Jiande sent envoys to establish friendly relations and stated his intention to come to his aid.

sentences.zh: 世充遣兄子琬、內史令長孫安世報，且乞師。

translations.literal: Shichong dispatched his nephew Wan and chief minister Changsun Anshi in reply, and also requested troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong sent his nephew Wan and chief minister Changsun Anshi in reply and also requested troops.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，青城宮守將以宮降，王進保之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, the garrison commander at Qingcheng Palace surrendered the palace, and the Prince advanced to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year, the garrison commander at Qingcheng Palace surrendered the palace, and the Prince of Qin advanced to occupy it.

sentences.zh: 世充引兵出方諸門，臨谷水以戰，王陣北邙，令屈突通步士五千逾水擊之。

translations.literal: Shichong led troops out through the Fangzhu Gate and fought along the Gu River; the Prince formed battle lines on Mount Beimang and ordered Qutu Tong to lead five thousand infantry across the water to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong led troops out through the Fangzhu Gate and fought along the Gu River; the Prince of Qin formed battle lines on Mount Beimang and ordered Qutu Tong to lead five thousand infantry across the water to attack.

sentences.zh: 兵接，王以騎決戰，世充排兵殊死鬥，自辰及午乃潰，俘斬八千人。

translations.literal: Once the armies clashed, the Prince decided the battle with cavalry; Shichong deployed his troops in a desperate fight, and only from the hour of chen until the hour of wu did they break — eight thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the armies clashed, the Prince decided the battle with cavalry; Wang Shichong deployed his troops in a desperate fight, and only from the hour of chen until the hour of wu did they break — eight thousand were captured or killed.

sentences.zh: 王傅城，塹而守之。

translations.literal: The Prince built fortifications around the city, dug moats, and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince built fortifications around the city, dug moats, and besieged it.

sentences.zh: 世充糧且盡，人相食，至以水汨泥去礫，取浮土糅米屑為餅。

translations.literal: Shichong's grain was nearly exhausted; people ate one another, even stirring muddy water to remove grit, scooping up the floating soil and mixing it with rice bran to make cakes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong's grain was nearly exhausted; people ate one another, even stirring muddy water to remove grit, scooping up the floating soil and mixing it with rice bran to make cakes.

sentences.zh: 民病腫股弱，相藉倚道上，其尚書郎盧君業、郭子高等皆餓死。

translations.literal: The people suffered swollen legs and weakness, leaning on one another along the roads; among them, Secretariat gentlemen Lu Junye, Guo Zigao, and others all died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered swollen legs and weakness, leaning on one another along the roads; among them, Secretariat gentlemen Lu Junye, Guo Zigao, and others all died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫鄭颋丐為浮屠，世充惡其言，殺之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Zheng Ting begged to become a Buddhist monk; Shichong hated his words and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Zheng Ting begged to become a Buddhist monk; Wang Shichong hated what he said and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 然氣竭，但嬰城須建德之救。

translations.literal: Yet his strength was spent; he could only hold the city and wait for Jiande's rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his strength was spent; he could only hold the city and wait for Dou Jiande's rescue.

sentences.zh: 五月，王禽建德，並獲王琬、長孫安世，俘示東都城下，且遣安世入言敗狀。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Prince captured Jiande, along with Wang Wan and Changsun Anshi; he displayed the prisoners beneath the walls of the Eastern Capital and sent Anshi inside to report their defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Prince of Qin captured Dou Jiande, along with Wang Wan and Changsun Anshi; he displayed the prisoners beneath the walls of the Eastern Capital and sent Anshi inside to report their defeat.

sentences.zh: 世充惶惑，將突圍出保襄、漢，謀於諸將，皆不答，遂率將吏降軍門。

translations.literal: Shichong was panic-stricken; he planned to break out and flee to Xiangyang and Hanzhong, but when he consulted his generals none responded, and he finally led his officers and officials to surrender at the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was panic-stricken; he planned to break out and flee to Xiangyang and Hanzhong, but when he consulted his generals none responded, and he finally led his officers and officials to surrender at the army gate.

sentences.zh: 王受之，以屬吏，陳兵入城，發府庫賚將士。

translations.literal: The Prince accepted the surrender, handed Shichong over to the officials, marched troops into the city, opened the treasuries, and rewarded the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince accepted the surrender, handed Wang Shichong over to the officials, marched troops into the city, opened the treasuries, and rewarded the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其黃門侍郎薛德音以移檄嫚逆，崔弘丹造弩多傷士，前誅之；

translations.literal: Earlier he had executed Palace Secretariat attendant Xue Deyin for issuing a proclamation that was insulting and rebellious, and Cui Hongdan for making crossbows that frequently injured the troops;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier he had executed Palace Secretariat attendant Xue Deyin for issuing a proclamation that was insulting and rebellious, and Cui Hongdan for making crossbows that frequently injured the troops;

sentences.zh: 又收段達、楊汪、孟孝義、單雄信、楊公卿、郭士衡、郭什柱、董浚、張童仁、硃粲、王德仁等斬洛渚上。

translations.literal: He also arrested Duan Da, Yang Wang, Meng Xiaoyi, Shan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shiheng, Guo Shizhu, Dong Jun, Zhang Tongren, Zhu Can, Wang Deren, and others, and executed them on the Luo River sandbar.
translations.idiomatic: He also arrested Duan Da, Yang Wang, Meng Xiaoyi, Shan Xiongxin, Yang Gongqing, Guo Shiheng, Guo Shizhu, Dong Jun, Zhang Tongren, Zhu Can, Wang Deren, and others, and executed them on the Luo River sandbar.

sentences.zh: 以世充歸長安，高祖數其罪，世充曰：「計臣罪不容誅，但秦王許臣以不死。」

translations.literal: Shichong was taken to Chang'an, and Emperor Gaozu enumerated his crimes; Shichong said: "I calculate that my crimes deserve death beyond pardon, but the Prince of Qin promised me I would not die.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong was taken to Chang'an, and Emperor Gaozu enumerated his crimes; Shichong said: "I know my crimes deserve death, but the Prince of Qin promised me I would not die.

sentences.zh: 乃赦為庶人，與其族徙於蜀。

translations.literal: He was pardoned and reduced to commoner status, and he and his clan were exiled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: He was pardoned and reduced to commoner status, and he and his clan were exiled to Shu.

sentences.zh: 將行，為羽林將軍獨孤修德所殺。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, he was killed by Yulin general Dugu Xiude.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, he was killed by Yulin general Dugu Xiude.

sentences.zh: 初，修德父機嘗仕越王侗，世充既篡，謀歸唐，為所屠者也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiude's father Ji had once served Prince Yue Yang Tong; after Shichong usurped the throne, Ji plotted to submit to Tang and was slaughtered by Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xiude's father Ji had once served Prince Yue Yang Tong; after Wang Shichong usurped the throne, Ji plotted to submit to Tang and was slaughtered by Shichong.

sentences.zh: 高祖免修德官。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu stripped Xiude of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu stripped Xiude of his office.

sentences.zh: 子玄應，兄世偉，在道謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Xuanying and his brother Shiwei plotted rebellion while en route and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanying and his brother Shiwei plotted rebellion while en route and were executed.

sentences.zh: 世充篡，凡三年滅。

translations.literal: From Shichong's usurpation to his destruction, three years in all elapsed.
translations.idiomatic: From Wang Shichong's usurpation to his destruction, three years elapsed in all.

sentences.zh: 竇建德竇建德，貝州漳南人。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande — Dou Jiande was a native of Zhangnan in Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande — Dou Jiande was a native of Zhangnan in Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 世為農，自言漢景帝太后父安成侯充之苗裔。

translations.literal: His family had been farmers for generations; he claimed to be a descendant of An Cheng Hou Chong, father of Empress Dowager Bo of Emperor Jing of Han.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been farmers for generations; he claimed to be a descendant of Marquis Cheng of An, father of Empress Dowager Bo of Emperor Jing of Han.

sentences.zh: 材力絕人，少重然許，喜俠節。

translations.literal: His physical strength was surpassing; in youth he greatly valued good faith and promises, and delighted in chivalrous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His physical strength was extraordinary; in youth he greatly valued keeping his word and delighted in chivalrous conduct.

sentences.zh: 鄉人喪親，貧無以葬，建德方耕，聞之太息，遽解牛與給喪事，鄉黨異之。

translations.literal: When a neighbor lost a parent and was too poor to bury them, Jiande was plowing in the fields; on hearing this he sighed deeply, immediately unhitched his ox and gave it for the funeral — the villagers marveled at this.
translations.idiomatic: When a neighbor lost a parent and was too poor to bury the body, Jiande was plowing in the fields; on hearing this he sighed deeply, immediately unhitched his ox and gave it for the funeral, and the villagers marveled at this.

sentences.zh: 盜夜劫其家，建德立戶下，盜入，擊三人死，余不敢進。

translations.literal: Robbers raided his home by night; Jiande stood beneath the doorway, and when the robbers entered he struck three dead and the rest dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers raided his home by night; Jiande stood beneath the doorway, and when the robbers entered he struck three dead and the rest dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 請其屍，建德曰：「可投繩系取之。」

translations.literal: They asked for the corpses; Jiande said: "You may throw a rope and tie them to haul them out.
translations.idiomatic: They asked for the corpses; Jiande said: "You may throw a rope and tie them to haul them out.

sentences.zh: 盜投繩，建德乃自縻，使盜曳出，躍起捉刀，復殺數人，繇是益知名。

translations.literal: The robbers threw the rope; Jiande then bound himself, had the robbers drag him out, leaped up, seized a blade, and killed several more — from this his fame grew still greater.
translations.idiomatic: The robbers threw the rope; Jiande then bound himself, had the robbers drag him out, leaped up, seized a blade, and killed several more — from this his fame grew still greater.

sentences.zh: 為裏長，犯法亡，會赦歸。

translations.literal: He served as village head, broke the law and fled, and returned when an amnesty was declared.
translations.idiomatic: He served as village head, broke the law and fled, and returned when an amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 久之，父卒，裏中送葬千余人，所贈予皆讓不受。

translations.literal: After some time his father died; more than a thousand people from the village attended the burial, but he declined every gift offered.
translations.idiomatic: After some time his father died; more than a thousand people from the village attended the burial, but he declined every gift offered.

sentences.zh: 隋大業七年，募兵伐遼東，建德補隊長。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Daye of Sui, when troops were being levied to campaign against Liaodong, Jiande was enrolled as a squad leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Daye of Sui, when troops were being levied to campaign against Liaodong, Jiande was enrolled as a squad leader.

sentences.zh: 方如軍，會邑人孫安祖盜羊，為縣令捕劾笞辱，安祖刺殺令，亡抵建德，建德陰舍之。

translations.literal: Just as he was about to join the army, a fellow townsman named Sun Anzu stole a sheep; the magistrate seized and flogged him in disgrace, and Anzu stabbed the magistrate to death and fled to Jiande, who secretly sheltered him.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to join the army, a fellow townsman named Sun Anzu stole a sheep; the magistrate seized and flogged him in disgrace, and Anzu stabbed the magistrate to death and fled to Jiande, who secretly sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 時山東饑，群盜起，乃謀曰：「往文皇帝時，天下盛強，發百萬眾伐遼東，猶為所敗。

translations.literal: At that time the east was suffering famine and bandits rose everywhere; they therefore plotted, saying: "In the time of Emperor Wen, when the realm was at its strongest, a million troops were sent against Liaodong and were still defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the east was suffering famine and bandits rose everywhere; they therefore plotted, saying: "In the time of Emperor Wen, when the realm was at its strongest, a million troops were sent against Liaodong and were still defeated.

sentences.zh: 今水潦為災，民力刓敝，主上不是恤，而親駕臨遼。

translations.literal: Now floods have brought disaster, the people's strength is exhausted and depleted, yet Our Lord does not look to their relief but personally leads the campaign to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Now floods have brought disaster, the people's strength is exhausted and depleted, yet the emperor does not look to their relief but personally leads the campaign to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 且往歲西征，十不一返，今創夷未平，又重發兵，人情危駭，易以搖動。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the western campaigns of past years, fewer than one in ten returned; wounds from war are not yet healed, and troops are being raised again — hearts are fearful and alarmed, and easily stirred to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the western campaigns of past years, fewer than one in ten returned; wounds from war are not yet healed, and troops are being raised again — hearts are fearful and alarmed, and easily stirred to rebellion.

sentences.zh: 丈夫不死，常建功於世，渠為亡命虜乎！

translations.literal: A true man, if he does not die, always achieves merit in the world — why should he be a hunted fugitive slave!
translations.idiomatic: A true man, if he does not die, always achieves merit in the world — why should he be a hunted fugitive slave!

sentences.zh: 我聞高雞泊廣袤數百里，葭薍阻奧，可以違難；

translations.literal: I have heard that Gaoji Marsh stretches hundreds of li in every direction, with reeds and rushes blocking the hidden depths — one can evade pursuit there;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Gaoji Marsh stretches hundreds of li in every direction, with reeds and rushes blocking the hidden depths — one can evade pursuit there;

sentences.zh: 承間竊出，椎埋掠奪，足以自資。

translations.literal: Seizing opportunities to slip out secretly, waylaying and plundering, one can support oneself well enough.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing opportunities to slip out secretly, waylaying and plundering, one can support oneself well enough.

sentences.zh: 因得聚豪傑，且觀時變，以就大計。」

translations.literal: Thus one may gather heroes and bold men, watch how the times change, and thereby accomplish a great design.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one may gather heroes and bold men, watch how the times change, and thereby accomplish a great design.

sentences.zh: 安祖然之。

translations.literal: Anzu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu agreed.

sentences.zh: 建德為招亡兵及民無產者數百，使安祖率之，入高雞為盜，安祖號「摸羊公」。

translations.literal: Jiande recruited several hundred deserters and landless commoners, had Anzu lead them, and entered Gaoji to become bandits; Anzu was called "the Sheep-Snatcher."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande recruited several hundred deserters and landless commoners, had Anzu lead them, and entered Gaoji to become bandits; Anzu was called "the Sheep-Snatcher."

sentences.zh: 時鄃人張金稱亦結眾萬余，依河渚間，蓚人高士達兵千余屯清河鄙上。

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Jincheng of Yucheng also gathered more than ten thousand followers and held the river banks; Gao Shida of Gaoyuan commanded more than a thousand troops encamped on the outskirts of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jincheng of Yucheng also gathered more than ten thousand followers and held the river banks; Gao Shida of Gaoyuan commanded more than a thousand troops encamped on the outskirts of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 諸盜往來漳南者多剽殺人，焚鄉聚，獨不入建德閭，郡縣意建德與賊通，捕族其家。

translations.literal: Bandits coming and going in the Zhangnan region mostly robbed and killed, burning villages — yet none entered Jiande's neighborhood; the commandery and county officials suspected Jiande was in league with the bandits and arrested and executed his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits coming and going in the Zhangnan region mostly robbed and killed, burning villages — yet none entered Jiande's neighborhood; the commandery and county officials suspected Jiande was in league with the bandits and arrested and executed his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 建德至河間，聞家屠滅，即率麾下二百人亡歸士達。

translations.literal: When Jiande reached Hejian and heard his family had been slaughtered, he immediately led his two hundred followers in flight back to Shida.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande reached Hejian and heard his family had been slaughtered, he immediately led his two hundred followers in flight back to Shida.

sentences.zh: 士達自稱東海公，以建德為司兵。

translations.literal: Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea and appointed Jiande as director of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shida styled himself Duke of the Eastern Sea and appointed Jiande as director of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 安祖為金稱所殺，其下數千人歸建德，眾益盛，至萬人，猶保高雞泊。

translations.literal: Anzu was killed by Jincheng, and his several thousand followers joined Jiande; his force grew still stronger, reaching ten thousand, and they still held Gaoji Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Anzu was killed by Jincheng, and his several thousand followers joined Jiande; his force grew still stronger, reaching ten thousand, and they still held Gaoji Marsh.

sentences.zh: 然傾身接物，其執苦與士卒均，由是能致人死力。

translations.literal: Yet he gave himself wholly in dealing with others and shared hardships equally with his soldiers; thereby he could summon from men their utmost devotion even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he gave himself wholly in dealing with others and shared hardships equally with his soldiers; thereby he could summon from men their utmost devotion even unto death.

sentences.zh: 十二年，涿郡通守郭絢率兵萬人討士達，士達自以智略不及建德，乃推為軍司馬，以兵屬焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Tongshou of Zhuo Commandery Guo Xuan led ten thousand troops against Shida; Shida, considering his own strategy inferior to Jiande's, promoted him to army marshal and placed the troops under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, Tongshou of Zhuo Commandery Guo Xuan led ten thousand troops against Shida; Shida, considering his own strategy inferior to Jiande's, promoted him to army marshal and placed the troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 建德既統眾，思用奇厭伏群盜，乃請士達守輜重，自以精兵七千迎絢，詐為亡狀。

translations.literal: Now that Jiande commanded the force, he wished to use a clever stratagem to overawe the other bandits; he asked Shida to guard the baggage train while he himself led seven thousand elite troops to meet Xuan, feigning a defeated flight.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jiande commanded the force, he wished to use a clever stratagem to overawe the other bandits; he asked Shida to guard the baggage train while he himself led seven thousand elite troops to meet Xuan, feigning a defeated flight.

sentences.zh: 士達取所虜，陽言建德妻子，殺之。

translations.literal: Shida took captives and falsely declared them to be Jiande's wife and children, and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shida took captives and falsely declared them to be Jiande's wife and children, and killed them.

sentences.zh: 建德遺絢書約降，請前驅執賊自效。

translations.literal: Jiande sent Xuan a letter offering surrender and asking to serve as vanguard in capturing the bandits to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande sent Xuan a letter offering surrender and asking to serve as vanguard in capturing the bandits to prove his loyalty.

sentences.zh: 絢信之，引兵從建德至長河界，欲與盟，兵懈不設備。

translations.literal: Xuan believed him, led his army following Jiande to the Changhe border, and intending to form an alliance, let his troops relax their guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan believed him, led his army following Jiande to the Changhe border, and intending to form an alliance, let his troops relax their guard.

sentences.zh: 建德襲殺其軍數千人，獲馬千匹，絢以數十騎去，追斬於平原，獻首士達，威振山東。

translations.literal: Jiande suddenly attacked and killed several thousand of his troops, seized a thousand horses; Xuan escaped with several dozen cavalry, was chased down and beheaded on the plain, his head presented to Shida — Jiande's prestige shook the entire east.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande suddenly attacked and killed several thousand of his troops and seized a thousand horses; Xuan escaped with several dozen cavalry but was chased down and beheaded on the plain, his head presented to Shida — Jiande's prestige shook the entire east.

sentences.zh: 隋遣太仆卿楊義臣討破張金稱於清河，殘黨畏誅，復屯嘯歸建德。

translations.literal: The Sui dispatched Minister of Imperial Studs Yang Yichen to defeat Zhang Jincheng at Qinghe; the remnant bands, fearing execution, gathered again and rallied to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dispatched Minister of Imperial Studs Yang Yichen to defeat Zhang Jincheng at Qinghe; the remnant bands, fearing execution, gathered again and rallied to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 義臣乘勝欲遂入高雞泊，窮劃根穴。

translations.literal: Yichen, riding his victory, wished to push on into Gaoji Marsh and thoroughly root out the lair.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen, riding his victory, wished to push on into Gaoji Marsh and thoroughly root out the lair.

sentences.zh: 建德謂士達曰：「隋善將獨義臣耳，新破金稱，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Jiande said to Shida: "Of Sui's able generals, Yichen alone matters; freshly victorious over Jincheng, his momentum cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said to Shida: "Of Sui's able generals, Yichen alone matters; freshly victorious over Jincheng, his momentum cannot be withstood.

sentences.zh: 宜引兵避之，彼欲戰不得，軍老食乏，乘之可有功。」

translations.literal: We ought to withdraw and avoid him; when he cannot obtain the battle he seeks, his army will age and food run short — strike then and success can be won.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to withdraw and avoid him; when he cannot obtain the battle he seeks, his army will grow weary and food run short — strike then and success can be won.

sentences.zh: 士達不納。

translations.literal: Shida did not accept this.
translations.idiomatic: Shida did not accept this.

sentences.zh: 留建德守壁，身將兵逆戰，置酒享士。

translations.literal: He left Jiande to guard the fortifications while he personally led troops to meet the enemy in battle, setting out wine to feast his men.
translations.idiomatic: He left Jiande to guard the fortifications while he personally led troops to meet the enemy in battle, setting out wine to feast his men.

sentences.zh: 建德聞，曰：「東海公未捷，遽自矜大，禍至不日矣。

translations.literal: When Jiande heard of this, he said: "The Duke of the Eastern Sea has not yet won a victory yet already prides himself so grandly — disaster will arrive within days.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiande heard of this, he said: "The Duke of the Eastern Sea has not yet won a victory yet already prides himself so grandly — disaster will arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 隋兵勝，必長驅而來，吾不能獨支。」

translations.literal: If the Sui army wins, it will surely come driving straight at us, and I cannot hold out alone.
translations.idiomatic: If the Sui army wins, it will surely come driving straight at us, and I cannot hold out alone.

sentences.zh: 乃留眾保壁，帥銳士據險待。

translations.literal: He therefore left the main force to hold the fortifications while he himself led crack troops to occupy a defensible position and wait.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore left the main force to hold the fortifications while he himself led crack troops to occupy a defensible position and wait.

sentences.zh: 後五日，義臣斬士達於陣，追北薄壘，守兵潰。

translations.literal: Five days later, Yichen cut down Shida in battle, pursued the retreating force right up to the ramparts, and the defending troops collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Five days later, Yichen cut down Shida in battle, pursued the retreating force right up to the ramparts, and the defending troops collapsed.

sentences.zh: 建德不能軍，以百余騎走饒陽，饒陽無備，因取之。

translations.literal: Jiande could not keep his army together; with a little over a hundred cavalry he fled to Raoyang, which was unprepared, and seized it.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande could not keep his army together; with a little over a hundred cavalry he fled to Raoyang, which was unprepared, and seized it.

sentences.zh: 義臣已殺士達，謂余黨不足憂，引去。

translations.literal: Yichen, having already killed Shida, judged the remnant bandits unworthy of concern and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yichen, having already killed Shida, judged the remnant bandits unworthy of concern and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 故建德得還平原，收士達士死胔葬焉。

translations.literal: Thus Jiande was able to return to Pingyuan, gathered Shida's dead soldiers, and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jiande was able to return to Pingyuan, gathered Shida's dead soldiers, and buried them.

sentences.zh: 為士達發喪，軍皆縞素。

translations.literal: He conducted funeral rites for Shida, and the entire army wore white mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted funeral rites for Shida, and the entire army wore white mourning.

sentences.zh: 招潰卒，得數千人，軍復振，自稱將軍。

translations.literal: He recruited scattered troops and gathered several thousand men; the army revived its strength, and he styled himself General.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited scattered troops and gathered several thousand men; the army revived its strength, and he styled himself General.

sentences.zh: 初，他盜得隋官及士人必殺之，唯建德恩遇甚備，引故饒陽長宋正本為客，尊任之，參決軍議。

translations.literal: At first, when other bandits captured Sui officials and literati they always killed them; only Jiande treated them with full favor, took the former Raoyang magistrate Song Zhengben as a guest-advisor, honored and entrusted him, and had him participate in deciding military policy.
translations.idiomatic: At first, other rebel bands invariably killed any Sui officials or scholars they captured. Jiande alone showed them every courtesy. He took on the former magistrate of Raoyang, Song Zhengben, as a retained adviser—honored him, relied on him, and brought him into deliberations on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 隋郡縣吏多以地歸之，勢益張，兵至十余萬。

translations.literal: Sui prefectural and county officials for the most part surrendered their territories to him; his power grew ever greater, and his forces reached more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sui officials across the prefectures and counties largely submitted their territories to him. His power swelled, and his army grew to more than a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 上谷賊王須拔自號「漫天王」，以兵略幽州，戰死。

translations.literal: The Shanggu bandit Wang Xuba styled himself "Heaven-Soaring King," raided Youzhou with his troops, and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuba, a rebel leader in Shanggu, proclaimed himself the "Heaven-Soaring King," led his forces against Youzhou, and was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 其下魏刀兒號「歷山飛」，壁深澤，眾十萬。

translations.literal: His subordinate Wei Dao'er styled himself "Flying Over Mount Li," walled himself in at Shenze, and had a host of a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His lieutenant Wei Dao'er took the title "Flying Over Mount Li," fortified himself at Shenze, and commanded a force of a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 建德以計襲取之，並有其地。

translations.literal: Jiande seized it from him by stratagem and took all his territory as well.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande captured him through a stratagem and absorbed his entire domain.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月，築壇場於河間樂壽，自立為長樂王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the thirteenth year, he built an altar at Leshou in Hejian and declared himself King of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year, he erected an altar at Leshou in Hejian and declared himself King of Changle.

sentences.zh: 十四年五月，更號夏王，建元丁丑，署官屬，分治郡縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year, he changed his title to King of Xia, established the era name Dingchou, appointed officials, and divided administration over prefectures and counties.
