translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourteenth year, he took the title King of Xia, proclaimed the Dingchou era, appointed a full bureaucracy, and organized rule over prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 七月，隋右翊衛將軍薛世雄督兵三萬討之，屯河間七里井，建德以勁兵伏旁澤中，悉拔諸城偽遁。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Sui Right Wing Guard General Xue Shixiong led thirty thousand troops against him and encamped at Qili Well in Hejian. Jiande hid crack troops in the marshes nearby and feigned retreat by abandoning all his cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, Xue Shixiong, the Sui Right Wing Guard General, marched against him with thirty thousand men and encamped at Qili Well in Hejian. Jiande concealed elite troops in the neighboring marshes and staged a false withdrawal, evacuating every city in his path.

sentences.zh: 世雄以為畏，稍弛備，建德率敢死士千人襲之。

translations.literal: Shixiong thought Jiande was afraid and relaxed his defenses slightly; Jiande led a thousand death-defying warriors in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong took this for fear and let his guard slip. Jiande then led a thousand men sworn to fight to the death in a sudden assault.

sentences.zh: 會大霧晝冥，跬不可視，隋軍驚，遂潰，相騰藉，死者如丘，世雄引數百騎亡去。

translations.literal: Just then a heavy fog darkened the day so that one could barely see a step ahead; the Sui army panicked and routed, trampling one another until the dead piled like mounds. Shixiong fled with several hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: A thick fog rolled in and turned day to night; men could scarcely see a foot ahead. The Sui army broke in panic, trampling one another until the dead lay heaped like hillocks. Shixiong escaped with only a few hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 盡得其眾，獲河間丞王琮，勞遣之。

translations.literal: He took all their troops and captured Hejian assistant prefect Wang Cong, treated him with honor, and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: He absorbed the entire enemy force and captured Wang Cong, the assistant prefect of Hejian, whom he treated with courtesy and then released.

sentences.zh: 琮復嬰城，建德進攻未下，而河間食盡，聞煬帝遇殺，琮率吏發喪，乘城大臨，建德遣使入吊，琮因請降。

translations.literal: Cong again held the city fast; Jiande pressed the attack but could not take it. When Hejian ran out of food and news arrived that Emperor Yang had been murdered, Cong led the officials in mourning rites, wept loudly from atop the walls, Jiande sent envoys to offer condolences, and Cong thereupon requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cong shut himself in the city once more, and Jiande's assault failed to break him. When Hejian's grain was exhausted and word came that Emperor Yang had been killed, Cong led his officials in funeral observances and wailed from the battlements. Jiande sent envoys to offer condolences, and Cong then asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 建德為退舍，飭饌具。

translations.literal: Jiande withdrew his camps and arranged a feast.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pulled his camps back and had a banquet prepared.

sentences.zh: 琮率郡屬素服面縛軍門，建德親釋徽纆，與言隋之亡，琮伏哭極哀，建德亦為泣。

translations.literal: Cong led the prefecture's officials in white hemp garments, bound, to the camp gate. Jiande personally untied his bonds, spoke with him of the fall of Sui, Cong prostrated himself and wept in deepest grief, and Jiande wept as well.
translations.idiomatic: Cong came to the camp gate in mourning white, his hands bound, at the head of the prefecture's officials. Jiande personally unbound him and spoke of the end of the Sui dynasty. Cong prostrated himself and wept in anguish—and Jiande wept with him.

sentences.zh: 麾下或言：「河間久拒守，多殺士，今力窮而下，請烹之。」

translations.literal: Some among his followers said: "Hejian resisted for so long and killed many of our men; now that their strength is exhausted and they surrender, please boil him alive.
translations.idiomatic: Some of his officers said: 「Hejian held out for so long and killed many of our men. Now that they are spent and have surrendered, boil him alive.」

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「琮，誼士也，吾方旌擢以勵事君者。

translations.literal: Jiande said: "Cong is a man of righteousness; I intend to honor and promote him to encourage those who serve their lord faithfully.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said: 「Cong is a man of integrity. I mean to honor and elevate him, to encourage those who remain loyal to their sovereign.」

sentences.zh: 且往為盜，可妄殺人，今將安百姓，定天下，而害忠臣乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, when we were bandits we could kill people at will; now that I would settle the people and pacify the realm, how could I harm a loyal minister?"
translations.idiomatic: When we were outlaws we could kill as we pleased—but now I mean to bring peace to the people and settle the realm. How could I harm a loyal minister?

sentences.zh: 即令其軍曰：「與琮隙者敢輒搖，罪三族！」

translations.literal: At once he commanded his army: "Whoever among you bears a grudge against Cong and dares so much as stir—your whole clan to the third degree shall be punished!"
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered his army: 「Anyone who bears a grudge against Cong and dares so much as lift a finger against him—his clan to the third degree shall be punished!」

sentences.zh: 乃授琮瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: He then appointed Cong prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Cong prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 始都樂壽，號金城宮，備百官，準開皇故事。

translations.literal: He first made Leshou his capital, naming the palace Jincheng; he fully staffed the bureaucracy according to the precedents of the Kaihuang era.
translations.idiomatic: He established his capital at Leshou, naming the palace Jincheng, filled out the ranks of government, and modeled his administration on the institutions of the Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 冬至，大會僚吏，有五大鳥集其宮，群鳥從之。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice he held a great assembly of his staff; five large birds alighted on his palace, and flocks of birds followed them.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice he convened a great gathering of his officials. Five enormous birds settled on his palace, and countless others followed in their wake.

sentences.zh: 又宗城人獻玄圭一，景城丞孔德紹曰：「昔天以是授禹，今瑞與之侔，國宜稱夏。」

translations.literal: Also a man of Zongcheng presented a black jade scepter. Jingcheng assistant prefect Kong Deshao said: "In ancient times Heaven bestowed this upon Yu; today the auspice matches it—the state ought to be called Xia.
translations.idiomatic: A man of Zongcheng also presented a black jade scepter. Kong Deshao, assistant prefect of Jingcheng, said: 「In antiquity Heaven gave this token to Yu the Great; the omen we see today equals that one. The realm should take the name Xia.」

sentences.zh: 建德然之。

translations.literal: Jiande agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande agreed.

sentences.zh: 改元五鳳，以德紹為內史侍郎。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Wufeng and made Deshao Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era name to Wufeng and appointed Deshao Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，宇文化及至魏縣，建德謂其納言宋正本及德紹曰：「吾，隋民也；

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, when Yuwen Huaji reached Wei County, Jiande said to his Chancellery Speaker Song Zhengben and Deshao: "I am a subject of Sui;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wude, when Yuwen Huaji reached Wei County, Jiande said to his Chancellery Speaker Song Zhengben and Deshao: 「I am a subject of Sui;

sentences.zh: 隋，吾君也。

translations.literal: Sui is my sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Sui is my sovereign.

sentences.zh: 今化及殺之，大逆不道，乃吾仇，欲為天下誅之，何如？」

translations.literal: Now Huaji has murdered him—a supreme crime against the Way and my enemy. I wish to execute him on behalf of the realm. What do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Now Huaji has murdered him—the gravest treason—and he is my enemy. I wish to punish him on behalf of the realm. What do you think?」

sentences.zh: 正本等曰：「大王奮布衣，起漳南，隋之列城莫不爭附者，以能杖順扶義、安四方也。

translations.literal: Zhengben and the others said: "Your Majesty rose from common cloth in Zhangnan; not a single walled city of Sui failed to rush to join you, because you wield righteous authority, uphold justice, and bring peace to the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengben and the others said: 「Your Majesty rose from humble cloth in Zhangnan, and every walled city of Sui raced to join you because you wield righteous authority, uphold justice, and bring peace to the four quarters.」

sentences.zh: 化及為隋姻裏，倚之不疑，今戕君而移其國，仇不共天，請鼓行執其罪。」

translations.literal: Huaji was related by marriage to the house of Sui and was trusted without suspicion; now he has slain his sovereign and stolen the state—enmity that cannot be shared under one heaven. We beg you to march at once and seize him for his crime."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was kin to the house of Sui by marriage and was trusted without reserve. Now he has murdered his sovereign and seized the realm—enmity that cannot be shared under one heaven. We beg you to march at once and bring him to justice.」

sentences.zh: 建德善之。

translations.literal: Jiande approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande approved.

sentences.zh: 即引兵討化及，連戰破之。

translations.literal: He immediately led troops against Huaji and repeatedly defeated him in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately marched against Huaji and defeated him in battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 化及保聊城，乃縱撞車機石，四面乘城，拔之。

translations.literal: Huaji held Liaocheng; Jiande deployed battering rams and stone-throwing engines, assaulted from all four sides scaling the walls, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji shut himself up in Liaocheng. Jiande brought up battering rams and catapults, assaulted the walls from every side, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 建德入，先謁蕭皇后，語稱臣。

translations.literal: Upon entering, Jiande first paid respects to Empress Xiao, addressing himself as her subject.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the city, Jiande first paid his respects to Empress Xiao, addressing himself as her subject.

sentences.zh: 執宇文智及、楊士覽、元武達、許弘仁、孟景等，召隋文武官共臨斬之，梟首轅門；

translations.literal: He seized Yuwen Zhiji, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, Meng Jing, and others, assembled Sui civil and military officials to witness their execution, and displayed their heads at the camp gate;
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yuwen Zhiji, Yang Shilan, Yuan Wuda, Xu Hongren, Meng Jing, and others, summoned Sui civil and military officials to witness their execution, and displayed their heads at the camp gate;

sentences.zh: 囚化及並其子，載以檻車，至大陸縣斬之。

translations.literal: He imprisoned Huaji along with his sons, loaded them in caged carts, and executed them at Dali County.
translations.idiomatic: He imprisoned Huaji and his sons, loaded them into caged carts, and executed them at Dali County.

sentences.zh: 建德性約素，不喜食肉，飯脫粟加蔬具，妻曹未嘗衣紈綺。

translations.literal: Jiande was by nature frugal and plain; he disliked eating meat, took husked millet with vegetables only, and his wife Lady Cao never wore silk gauze or brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was austere by nature. He avoided meat, ate husked millet with plain vegetables, and his wife Lady Cao never wore silk.

sentences.zh: 及為王，妾侍裁十數。

translations.literal: Even after becoming king, his consorts numbered barely a dozen.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he became king, his concubines numbered barely a dozen.

sentences.zh: 每下城破敵，貲寶並散賚將士。

translations.literal: Whenever he captured a city or defeated an enemy, he distributed all treasure and goods as rewards to his officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he took a city or defeated an enemy, he distributed all treasure and booty among his officers and men.

sentences.zh: 至是，得隋宮人尚千數，悉放去；

translations.literal: On this occasion he obtained more than a thousand Sui palace women and released them all;
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion he obtained more than a thousand women from the Sui palace and released them all;

sentences.zh: 其文武、驍果尚萬余，各聽所之。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand civil and military officials and elite troops were each allowed to go where they wished.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand civil and military officials and elite warriors were each free to go wherever they chose.

sentences.zh: 乃以誅化及報越王侗，侗封之夏王，遂號大夏。

translations.literal: He then reported Huaji's execution to Prince of Yue Yang Tong; Tong enfeoffed him as King of Xia, and he thereupon styled his state Great Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported Huaji's execution to Yang Tong, Prince of Yue, who enfeoffed him as King of Xia; he thereupon styled his state Great Xia.

sentences.zh: 以隋黃門侍郎裴矩為尚書右仆射，兵部侍郎崔君肅為侍中，少府令何稠為工部尚書，余隨才署職，委以政事。

translations.literal: He appointed former Sui Director of the Yellow Gate Pei Ju as Vice Minister of the Right of the Ministry of State, Vice Minister of War Cui Junsu as Palace Attendant, Director of the Palace Bureau He Chou as Minister of Works, and assigned the rest according to talent, entrusting them with administration.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the former Sui Director of the Yellow Gate, Pei Ju, as Vice Minister of the Right; the Vice Minister of War, Cui Junsu, as Palace Attendant; the Director of the Palace Bureau, He Chou, as Minister of Works; and assigned the rest according to their abilities, entrusting them with the affairs of government.

sentences.zh: 有願往關中及東都者，恣聽不留，仍給道裏費，以兵護出於境。

translations.literal: Those who wished to go to Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital were freely permitted to leave without being detained; travel expenses were still granted, and troops escorted them beyond the border.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to go to Guanzhong or the Eastern Capital were free to leave without hindrance; he still provided travel expenses and sent troops to escort them beyond his borders.

sentences.zh: 二年，陷邢、趙、滄三州。

translations.literal: In the second year he captured the three prefectures of Xing, Zhao, and Cang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he captured the three prefectures of Xing, Zhao, and Cang.

sentences.zh: 復陷冀州，執刺史曲棱，赦之，復以為刺史。

translations.literal: He again took Jizhou, seized Prefect Qu Ling, pardoned him, and reappointed him prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He again took Jizhou, captured Prefect Qu Ling, pardoned him, and restored him to office.

sentences.zh: 八月，陷洺州，虜刺史袁子幹，遂遷都焉，更號萬春宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he took Luozhou, captured Prefect Yuan Zigan, moved his capital there, and renamed the palace Wanchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he took Luozhou, captured Prefect Yuan Zigan, moved his capital there, and renamed the palace Wanchun.

sentences.zh: 使人如灌津祠先墓，置守冢三十家。

translations.literal: He sent men to Guanjin to sacrifice at his ancestors' tombs and stationed thirty households to guard the graves.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men to Guanjin to offer sacrifices at his ancestors' tombs and posted thirty households to tend the graves.

sentences.zh: 又遣使朝侗，因與王世充結歡，北聘突厥，士馬益精雄。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to court Yang Tong and thereby established friendly ties with Wang Shichong; he sent a diplomatic mission north to the Turks, and his troops and horses grew ever more formidable.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent envoys to pay court to Yang Tong and thereby established friendly relations with Wang Shichong; he dispatched a diplomatic mission north to the Turks, and his troops and horses grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 俄而世充廢侗，乃絕之。

translations.literal: Before long Shichong deposed Tong, and Jiande broke off relations with him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Shichong deposed Yang Tong, and Jiande severed relations with him.

sentences.zh: 始建天子旌旗，出入警蹕，書稱詔。

translations.literal: He began to raise the imperial banner, travel with guard detachments clearing the road, and style his edicts as imperial decrees.
translations.idiomatic: He began to raise the imperial standard, travel with road-clearing guards, and style his written orders as imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 追謚隋煬帝為閔帝，以齊王暕子政道為鄖公。

translations.literal: He posthumously honored Emperor Yang as Emperor Min and installed Prince of Qi Yang Zhao's son Zhengdao as Duke of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored Emperor Yang as Emperor Min and installed Zhengdao, son of Prince of Qi Yang Zhao, as Duke of Yun.

sentences.zh: 義成公主在突厥，遣使迎蕭後，建德自將千余騎送之，並獻化及首。

translations.literal: Princess Yicheng was among the Turks; he sent envoys to welcome Empress Xiao. Jiande personally led more than a thousand cavalry to escort her and also presented Huaji's head.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Yicheng was among the Turks; he sent envoys to welcome Empress Xiao. Jiande personally led more than a thousand horsemen to escort her and also presented Yuwen Huaji's head.

sentences.zh: 未幾，連突厥侵相州，刺史呂瑉死之。

translations.literal: Before long, joining with the Turks he raided Xiangzhou; Prefect Lu Min died defending it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, allied with the Turks, he invaded Xiangzhou; Prefect Lu Min died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 進攻衛州，執河北大使淮安王神通、同安長公主、黎陽守將李世勣，釋之。

translations.literal: He advanced on Weizhou and seized the Hebei Grand Ambassador Prince Huai'an Wang Shentong, the Princess of Tong'an, and Li Shiji, garrison commander of Liyang, then released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Weizhou and captured Prince Huai'an Wang Shentong, the Hebei Grand Ambassador, the Princess of Tong'an, and Li Shiji, the garrison commander of Liyang—then released them all.

sentences.zh: 復使世勣守黎陽，館王、公主，饋以客禮。

translations.literal: He again placed Shiji in charge of Liyang, housed the prince and princess as guests, and entertained them with the courtesies due to honored visitors.
translations.idiomatic: He restored Li Shiji to command at Liyang, lodged the prince and princess as guests, and treated them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 滑州刺史王軌為奴所殺，奴以首奔建德，建德曰：「奴殺主，大逆。

translations.literal: Prefect Wang Gui of Huazhou was killed by his slave; the slave brought Gui's head to Jiande. Jiande said: "A slave who kills his master is guilty of supreme treason.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, prefect of Huazhou, was killed by his slave, who brought Gui's head to Jiande. Jiande said: 「A slave who kills his master commits the gravest treason.

sentences.zh: 納之不可不賞，賞逆則廢教，將焉用為？」

translations.literal: To accept him one cannot fail to reward him, yet to reward treachery is to abolish moral instruction—of what use would such a man be?
translations.idiomatic: To shelter him I must reward him—but to reward treachery is to destroy all moral teaching. Of what use would such a man be?」

sentences.zh: 命斬奴而返軌首，滑人德之，遂降，齊、濟二州亦降。

translations.literal: He ordered the slave beheaded and returned Gui's head; the people of Huazhou were grateful and submitted. Qi and Ji prefectures also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the slave beheaded and returned Wang Gui's head. The people of Huazhou were grateful and submitted, and the prefectures of Qi and Ji followed suit.

sentences.zh: 兗賊徐圓朗聞風送款。

translations.literal: The Yan bandit Xu Yuanlang, hearing of this, sent envoys offering submission.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuanlang, a rebel leader in Yan, sent envoys offering submission upon hearing the news.

sentences.zh: 三年，世勣自拔歸國，吏白建德誅其父，建德曰：「臣勣，唐臣，不忘其主，忠也。

translations.literal: In the third year Shiji broke free and returned to the Tang realm. Officials reported to Jiande that his father should be executed. Jiande said: "Shiji is a Tang minister who does not forget his lord—that is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Shiji broke free and returned to Tang territory. Officials urged Jiande to execute his father. Jiande said: 「Shiji is a Tang minister who does not forget his sovereign—that is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 父何罪？」

translations.literal: What crime has his father committed?
translations.idiomatic: What crime has his father committed?」

sentences.zh: 釋不問。

translations.literal: He released the father without further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: He released the father without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 高祖遣使修好，建德即以公主等歸京師。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys seeking cordial relations; Jiande at once sent the princess and the others back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu sent envoys seeking friendly relations, and Jiande at once sent the princess and the others back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 嘗執趙州刺史張誌昂、邢州刺史陳君賓、大使張道源等，將殺之，國之祭酒淩敬諫曰：「夫犬吠非其主，彼悉力堅守，以窮就禽，伏節士也。

translations.literal: Once he had seized Prefect Zhang Zhiao of Zhao, Prefect Chen Junbin of Xing, and Grand Ambassador Zhang Daoyuan, and was about to execute them, when National University Libationer Ling Jing remonstrated: "A dog barks not at its own master—those men exhausted every effort in stubborn defense and were captured only when utterly exhausted; they are men who kept their integrity unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had captured Zhang Zhiao, prefect of Zhao, Chen Junbin, prefect of Xing, and Grand Ambassador Zhang Daoyuan, and was about to execute them, National University Libationer Ling Jing remonstrated: 「A dog barks only at strangers—those men defended to the last and were taken only when utterly spent. They are men who died for their principles.」

sentences.zh: 今殺之，無以勸。」

translations.literal: To kill them now would offer no encouragement to others.
translations.idiomatic: To kill them now would offer no encouragement to others.」

sentences.zh: 建德怒曰：「我傅其城，猶不下，勞費士旅，何可赦？」

translations.literal: Jiande angrily said: "I invested their cities and they still would not submit, wasting the blood and labor of my soldiers—how could they be pardoned?"
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said angrily: 「I besieged their cities and they still would not yield, wasting the blood and toil of my soldiers—how can they be pardoned?」

sentences.zh: 敬曰：「王之大將高士興抗羅藝於易南，兵未交，士興即降，王以為可乎？」

translations.literal: Ling said: "Your Majesty's great general Gao Shixing fought Luo Yi south of Yi—before the armies had even joined battle Shixing surrendered. Would Your Majesty have considered that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Ling said: 「Your Majesty's great general Gao Shixing faced Luo Yi south of Yi—before the armies had even clashed, Shixing surrendered. Would Your Majesty have found that acceptable?」

sentences.zh: 建德悟，即釋之。

translations.literal: Jiande understood, and immediately released them.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande saw the point and immediately released them.

sentences.zh: 然其大將王伏寶數持兵，功略在諸帥上，或讒其反，建德殺之。

translations.literal: Yet his great general Wang Fubao repeatedly carried troops into the field; his achievements and conquests ranked above the other commanders. Some slandered him as plotting rebellion, and Jiande had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his great general Wang Fubao had led troops again and again, and his achievements outshone those of every other commander. Some accused him of plotting rebellion, and Jiande had him executed.

sentences.zh: 伏寶臨死呼曰：「我無罪，王何信讒，自刈左右手乎？」

translations.literal: At the point of death Fubao cried out: "I am innocent—why does Your Majesty trust slander and cut off your own right and left hands?
translations.idiomatic: At the point of death Fubao cried out: 「I am innocent—why does Your Majesty trust slander and cut off your own right and left hands?」

sentences.zh: 後戰數不利。

translations.literal: Afterward his battles went poorly again and again.
translations.idiomatic: After that his battles went badly again and again.

sentences.zh: 九月，建德自帥師圍幽州，為羅藝所敗，藝乘勝襲其營，建德陣營中，填塹而出，敗藝眾，進薄其城，不能拔，乃還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jiande personally led an army to besiege Youzhou and was defeated by Luo Yi. Yi pressed his victory and raided Jiande's camp. Jiande stood in battle formation within his camp, filled in the moat, and broke out; he defeated Yi's force, advanced close to his walls but could not take the city, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jiande personally led an army to besiege Youzhou and was defeated by Luo Yi. Yi pressed his advantage and raided Jiande's camp. Jiande formed battle lines within his encampment, filled in the moat, and broke out; he routed Yi's force, pressed close to the city walls but could not take them, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 濟陰賊孟海公兵三萬，據周橋城以掠河南，建德自擊之。

translations.literal: The Jiyin bandit Meng Haigong commanded thirty thousand troops, held Zhouqiao Fort, and plundered Henan; Jiande attacked him in person.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Haigong, a rebel leader in Jiyin, commanded thirty thousand men, held Zhouqiao Fort, and plundered Henan; Jiande attacked him in person.

sentences.zh: 會秦王伐東都，其中書舍人劉斌獻說曰：「唐據關內，鄭王河南，夏有冀方，此鼎足相持勢也。

translations.literal: Just then the Prince of Qin was campaigning against the Eastern Capital. Liu Bin, a Secretariat drafting officer, offered a plan: "Tang holds Guanzhong, the Prince of Zheng holds Henan, and Xia holds the Ji region—this is the posture of three legs of a tripod mutually balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Prince of Qin was campaigning against the Eastern Capital. Liu Bin, a drafting officer of the Secretariat, offered a plan: 「Tang holds Guanzhong, the Prince of Zheng holds Henan, and Xia holds the Ji region—this is the posture of three powers balanced like the legs of a tripod.」

sentences.zh: 今唐悉兵臨鄭，出入二年，鄭人日蹙。

translations.literal: Now Tang has mustered its full strength against Zheng; for two years troops have come and gone, and the people of Zheng are daily driven tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Now Tang has thrown its full strength against Zheng; for two years the armies have surged back and forth, and the people of Zheng grow more desperate by the day.

sentences.zh: 二國兵不解，唐強鄭弱，勢必舉鄭，鄭滅則大夏有齒寒之憂。

translations.literal: With both states' armies locked in combat, Tang is strong and Zheng is weak; Tang is certain to take Zheng. When Zheng falls, Great Xia will face the worry of chilled teeth.
translations.idiomatic: With both armies locked in combat, Tang is strong and Zheng is weak; Tang is bound to take Zheng. When Zheng falls, Great Xia will face the same peril as teeth exposed when the lips are gone.

sentences.zh: 為大王計，莫若援鄭，使鄭抗其內，我攻其外，唐之兵必卻，唐卻而鄭完，然後徐觀其變。

translations.literal: For Your Majesty's plan, nothing surpasses aiding Zheng—let Zheng resist them within while we strike from without; Tang's army will surely retreat. Once Tang withdraws and Zheng is intact, then observe how matters shift at leisure.
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty's plan, nothing surpasses aiding Zheng—let Zheng hold them at bay from within while we strike from without; Tang's army will surely fall back. Once Tang withdraws and Zheng is intact, then watch how matters unfold at leisure.

sentences.zh: 鄭若可圖，因而取之，並二國兵，乘唐師老，長驅而西，關中可遂有也。」

translations.literal: If Zheng can be taken, seize the opportunity and absorb it; unite the forces of both states, and while Tang's army is exhausted drive west at full speed—the Guanzhong region can then be possessed.
translations.idiomatic: If Zheng can be taken, seize the opportunity and absorb it; unite the forces of both states, and while Tang's army is exhausted drive west at full speed—Guanzhong can then be yours.

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「善。」

translations.literal: Jiande said: "Well said."
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said: 「Well said.」

sentences.zh: 乃遣使聘世充，與連和，會世充亦自乞師，即令其臣李大師、魏處繪來朝，請解鄭圍，秦王留之不答。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to Wang Shichong to propose an alliance. It happened that Shichong also begged for troops; Jiande had his ministers Li Dashshi and Wei Chuhui come to court and request that the siege of Zheng be lifted. The Prince of Qin detained them and gave no answer.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent envoys to Wang Shichong to propose an alliance. Wang Shichong had also begged for reinforcements, so Jiande had his ministers Li Dashshi and Wei Chuhui come to court and request that the siege of Zheng be lifted. The Prince of Qin detained them and gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 四年，建德克周橋，虜海公，留其將範願戍之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jiande captured Zhouqiao, took Haigong prisoner, and left his general Fan Yuan to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Jiande captured Zhouqiao, took Meng Haigong prisoner, and left his general Fan Yuan to garrison the fort.

sentences.zh: 悉發海公、徐圓朗之眾，並兵號三十萬救世充，至滑州，世充行臺仆射韓弘開城納之。

translations.literal: He mustered the forces of Haigong and Xu Yuanlang; combined, the army numbered three hundred thousand to rescue Wang Shichong. At Huazhou, Shichong's mobile secretariat vice director Han Hong opened the gates and admitted him.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered the forces of Meng Haigong and Xu Yuanlang; combined, the army numbered three hundred thousand to rescue Wang Shichong. At Huazhou, Han Hong, vice director of Wang Shichong's mobile secretariat, opened the gates and admitted him.

sentences.zh: 建德進逼元、梁、管三州，皆陷，遂屯滎陽。

translations.literal: Jiande pressed forward and took the three prefectures of Yuan, Liang, and Guan, then encamped at Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande pressed forward and captured the three prefectures of Yuan, Liang, and Guan, then encamped at Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 運糧溯河西上，舟相屬不絕。

translations.literal: Supply grain was transported upriver on the west bank; boats stretched in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Grain supplies were transported upriver along the west bank, boats stretching in an unbroken line.

sentences.zh: 壁成臯東原，築營板渚。

translations.literal: He walled himself on the eastern plateau of Chenggao and built fortified camps at Banzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified himself on the eastern plateau of Chenggao and built camps at Banzhu.

sentences.zh: 遣使與世充約期，又遺秦王以書。

translations.literal: He sent envoys to fix a date with Shichong and also sent a letter to the Prince of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to fix a rendezvous with Wang Shichong and also sent a letter to the Prince of Qin.

sentences.zh: 三月，王進據虎牢。

translations.literal: In the third month the Prince advanced and took Tiger Trap Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Prince of Qin advanced and seized Tiger Trap Pass.

sentences.zh: 翌日，以騎五百覘建德營，設伏道側，獨以數騎去賊營三里，覺，賊出騎追之，王漸卻，誘至伏所，卒起奮擊。

translations.literal: The next day, with five hundred cavalry he reconnoitered Jiande's camp, set an ambush by the roadside, and with only a handful of riders went three li from the rebel camp. When detected, rebel cavalry pursued; the Prince gradually withdrew, luring them to the ambush, then sprang up and struck fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, with five hundred horsemen he reconnoitered Jiande's camp, set an ambush by the roadside, and with only a few riders rode to within three li of the enemy camp. When spotted, enemy cavalry gave chase; the Prince slowly withdrew, luring them to the ambush, then sprang up and struck with full force.

sentences.zh: 賊騎驚，引去，追斬三百級，獲其將殷秋、石瓚，乃報建德以書。

translations.literal: The rebel cavalry panicked and withdrew; three hundred were killed in pursuit. Generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan were captured, and the Prince sent a letter in reply to Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cavalry panicked and fled; three hundred were cut down in pursuit. Generals Yin Qiu and Shi Zan were captured, and the Prince sent a letter in reply to Jiande.

sentences.zh: 建德失二將，又聞唐兵精，得書猶豫，頓六十日不敢西。

translations.literal: Jiande had lost two generals; hearing that Tang troops were elite, upon receiving the letter he hesitated. He halted sixty days without daring to advance west.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande had lost two generals; hearing that Tang troops were formidable, he hesitated upon receiving the letter and halted for sixty days without daring to advance west.

sentences.zh: 時世充弟世辯為徐州行臺，亦遣將郭士衡、兵數千人從建德，王遣王君廓以輕騎抄其饟，執賊大將張清特。

translations.literal: At the time Shichong's brother Shibian was mobile secretariat at Xuzhou; he also sent General Guo Shiheng with several thousand troops to accompany Jiande. The Prince dispatched Wang Jungkuo with light cavalry to raid their grain supply and captured the rebel general Zhang Qingte.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Shichong's brother Shibian served as mobile secretariat at Xuzhou; he also sent General Guo Shiheng with several thousand troops to join Jiande. The Prince of Qin dispatched Wang Jungkuo with light cavalry to raid their grain supply and captured the enemy general Zhang Qingte.

sentences.zh: 建德懼，人情攜駭，其諸將又新破海公，掠獲盈給，日夜思歸。

translations.literal: Jiande grew fearful; morale split and shook; his generals, having recently defeated Haigong, were laden with plunder and thought only of going home day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande grew fearful; morale splintered and panic spread. His generals, having recently defeated Meng Haigong, were laden with plunder and thought of nothing but going home.

sentences.zh: 淩敬說建德曰：「今唐以重兵圍東都，守虎牢，我若悉兵濟河，取懷州河陽，以重將戍之，然後鳴鼓建旗，逾太行，入上黨，傳檄旁郡，進壺口以駭蒲津，收河東地，此上策也。

translations.literal: Ling Jing urged Jiande: "Today Tang has heavy forces besieging the Eastern Capital while holding Tiger Trap; if we concentrate our army to cross the Yellow River, take Huaizhou and Heyang, garrison them with trusted generals, then beat drums and raise banners, cross the Taihang range, enter Shangdang, dispatch proclamations to neighboring commanderies, advance on Hukou to threaten Pujin Ferry, and recover the Hedong region—that is the supreme strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ling Jing urged Jiande: 「Today Tang has heavy forces besieging the Eastern Capital while holding Tiger Trap Pass. If we concentrate our army, cross the Yellow River, take Huaizhou and Heyang, and garrison them with trusted generals, then beat drums and raise banners, cross the Taihang range, enter Shangdang, dispatch proclamations to neighboring commanderies, advance on Hukou to threaten Pujin Ferry, and recover the Hedong region—that is the supreme strategy.

sentences.zh: 且有三利：乘虛扌壽境，師有萬全，一也；

translations.literal: Moreover there are three advantages: taking advantage of their exposure to raid their territory, the army enjoys complete security—that is the first;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover there are three advantages: striking while they are exposed to raid their territory, so the army enjoys complete security—that is the first;

sentences.zh: 拓土得眾，二也；

translations.literal: expanding territory and gaining followers—that is the second;
translations.idiomatic: expanding territory and gaining followers—that is the second;

sentences.zh: 鄭圍自解，三也。」

translations.literal: the siege of Zheng would lift of itself—that is the third.
translations.idiomatic: the siege of Zheng would lift of itself—that is the third.」

sentences.zh: 建德將從之，而王琬、長孫安世日請兵西，每言必流涕，又陰賫金玉啗諸將，以撓其謀。

translations.literal: Jiande was about to follow this advice, but Wang Wan and Zhangsun Anshi daily pleaded for troops to go west, weeping each time they spoke; they also secretly sent gold and jade to bribe the generals to thwart the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was about to follow this advice, but Wang Wan and Zhangsun Anshi daily pleaded for troops to march west, weeping each time they spoke; they also secretly sent gold and jade to bribe the generals and thwart the plan.

sentences.zh: 眾乃曰：「淩敬書生，豈知戰？」

translations.literal: The officers then said: "Ling Jing is a bookish man—what does he know of war?
translations.idiomatic: The officers then said: 「Ling Jing is a bookish man—what does he know of war?」

sentences.zh: 建德乃謝曰：「今士心銳，天贊我也，師將大捷。

translations.literal: Jiande accordingly apologized: "Now the troops' spirit is sharp; Heaven is aiding me—the campaign will win a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande accordingly apologized: 「Now the troops' spirit is sharp; Heaven is on my side—the campaign will bring a great victory.

sentences.zh: 方用眾議，不得如公言。」

translations.literal: I must follow the consensus of the officers and cannot act as you advise.
translations.idiomatic: I must follow the consensus of the officers and cannot act as you advise.」

sentences.zh: 敬固爭，建德怒，命扶出。

translations.literal: Jing argued stubbornly; Jiande grew angry and ordered him carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Jing pressed his argument, but Jiande flew into a rage and had him carried out of the hall.

sentences.zh: 其妻諫曰：「祭酒計甚善，王盍用之？

translations.literal: His wife remonstrated, saying, "The director of studies' plan is very good — why does Your Majesty not adopt it?
translations.idiomatic: His wife urged him, saying, 「The director of studies' plan is excellent — why not adopt it?

sentences.zh: 夫自滏口道乘唐之虛，連營漸進以取山北，因招突厥西抄關中，唐必還師自救，鄭難紓矣。

translations.literal: By the Fuyu Pass route one could exploit Tang's weakness, advance camp by camp to take the lands north of the mountains, and meanwhile summon the Turks to raid Guanzhong from the west — Tang would surely return its army to save itself, and Zheng's peril would be eased.
translations.idiomatic: March through the Fuyu Pass while Tang is exposed, advance camp by camp to seize the northern hills, and call in the Turks to strike Guanzhong from the west. Tang will have to turn back to save itself, and Zheng's siege will be lifted.

sentences.zh: 今頓兵虎牢下，徒自苦，恐無功。」

translations.literal: Now to halt the army below Tiger Trap Pass is only to torment ourselves — I fear there will be no success.
translations.idiomatic: To sit idle below Tiger Trap Pass is only to wear ourselves down, and I fear we shall accomplish nothing.」

sentences.zh: 建德曰：「此非女子所知。

translations.literal: Jiande said, "This is not something a woman can understand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande said, 「That is not for a woman to judge.

sentences.zh: 且鄭朝暮待吾來，既許之，豈可見難而退，且示天下不信。」

translations.literal: Moreover Zheng awaits us morning and evening; since I have already promised, how can I withdraw at the first difficulty and show the realm that I am not to be trusted?」
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Zheng has been waiting on us day and night. I have given my word — how can I turn back at the first hard fight and show the world I cannot be trusted?」

translations.literal: (Closing quotation mark.)
translations.idiomatic: (End of Jiande's reply.)

sentences.zh: 五月，建德自板渚出為陣，西薄汜南，屬鵲山，亙二十里，鼓而前。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Jiande marched out from Banzhu to form battle lines, pressed west to the south of Sishui, ranged along Magpie Hill for twenty li, and advanced to the beat of drums.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jiande marched out from Banzhu, drew up his lines west of the south Sishui, stretched twenty li along Magpie Hill, and advanced to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 郭士衡為遊兵。

translations.literal: Guo Shiheng commanded the skirmishers.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Shiheng led the skirmishing force.

sentences.zh: 秦王登虎牢城望其軍，按甲不戰，曰：「賊起山東，未嘗見大敵，今度險士囂，令不肅也；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin ascended the walls of Tiger Trap to view their army, held his troops in check and would not give battle, and said, "These bandits rose in Shandong and have never faced a great enemy; now, having crossed difficult terrain, their soldiers are arrogant and their discipline slack;
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin climbed the walls of Tiger Trap to watch them, kept his men under arms but refused battle, and said, 「These rebels came out of Shandong and have never met a real army. After a hard march their men are cocky and slack —

sentences.zh: 逼城而陣，有輕我心。

translations.literal: to press close to the city and deploy in battle array shows they hold me in contempt.
translations.idiomatic: to camp right under our walls shows they despise us.

sentences.zh: 待其饑，破之果矣。」

translations.literal: Wait until they are hungry, and breaking them will be certain.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until hunger sets in, and we shall break them for certain.」

sentences.zh: 日中，建德士皆坐列，渴爭飲，意益怠。

translations.literal: At midday Jiande's soldiers all sat in their ranks, quarreling over drink in their thirst, and grew still more slack in spirit.
translations.idiomatic: By midday Jiande's men were sitting in their ranks, quarreling over water in the heat, and growing ever more careless.

sentences.zh: 王麾軍先登，騎怒，塵大漲，乃率史大奈、秦叔寶纏麾幟，弛出賊陣後，建德軍顧而驚，遂大潰。

translations.literal: The Prince waved his army forward to climb first; the cavalry charged, dust billowed high; he then led Shi Dana and Qin Shubao to wind around the enemy standards and gallop out behind their battle line. Jiande's army looked back in alarm and was utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince signaled the advance. His cavalry thundered forward in a rising cloud of dust. He led Shi Dana and Qin Shubao in a sweep around the enemy standards and burst out behind their line. Jiande's army looked back in panic and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 建德被重創，竄牛口谷。

translations.literal: Jiande was badly wounded and fled into Ox Mouth Gorge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande was badly wounded and fled into Ox Mouth Gorge.

sentences.zh: 車騎將軍白士讓、楊武威獲之，傳而西，斬長安市，年四十九。

translations.literal: The chariot-and-cavalry generals Bai Shirang and Yang Wuwei captured him; he was sent westward and executed in Chang'an City at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Chariot-and-cavalry generals Bai Shirang and Yang Wuwei seized him. He was sent west and beheaded in Chang'an at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 初，其軍有謠曰：「豆入牛口，勢不得久。」

translations.literal: Earlier there had been a song in his army: "When the bean enters the ox's mouth, its force cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: There had been a saying in his army: 「When the bean enters the ox's mouth, its power cannot endure.」

sentences.zh: 至是果敗。

translations.literal: Now at last he was indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Now the prophecy was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 建德妻與其左仆射齊善行以騎數百遁還洺州。

translations.literal: Jiande's wife and his left vice premier Qi Shanshang fled with several hundred horsemen back to Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande's wife and his left vice premier Qi Shanshang escaped with a few hundred horsemen back to Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 余黨欲立其養子為主，善行曰：「夏王奄定河朔，號為威強，今一出不復，非天命有歸哉？

translations.literal: The remaining faction wished to set up his foster son as ruler; Shanshang said, "The King of Xia swiftly pacified Hebei, and was called formidable and strong; now with one sortie he did not return — is this not Heaven's mandate finding its home?
translations.idiomatic: The survivors wanted to set up his foster son as ruler. Shanshang said, 「The King of Xia had all but pacified Hebei and was feared as invincible. One campaign, and he never came back — has not Heaven chosen its lord?

sentences.zh: 不如委心請命，無為塗炭生民也！」

translations.literal: Better to surrender wholeheartedly and not make the common people suffer in fire and ash!
translations.idiomatic: Better to submit in good faith than drag the people through fire and ruin!」

sentences.zh: 遂分府庫散給將士，令各解去。

translations.literal: He then divided the treasury stores and distributed them to the officers and soldiers, ordering each to disband and go his way.
translations.idiomatic: He divided the treasury among the officers and soldiers and told them to disband and go home.

sentences.zh: 善行乃與右仆射裴矩、行臺曹旦率官屬及建德妻奉山東地並傳國八璽來降。

translations.literal: Shanshang then, with the right vice premier Pei Ju and the mobile secretariat Cao Dan, led the officials and Jiande's wife to surrender the lands east of the mountains together with the eight imperial seals of transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshang then, with right vice premier Pei Ju and mobile secretariat Cao Dan, led the officials and Jiande's wife to surrender the eastern provinces and the eight imperial seals of transmission.

sentences.zh: 建德起兵至滅凡六年。

translations.literal: From Jiande's raising of troops to his destruction was six years in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Jiande raised his banner to his fall was six years in all.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：煬帝失德，天醜其為，生人辜，群盜乘之，如蝟毛而奮。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Emperor Yang lost virtue; Heaven was revolted by his conduct; living men bore the guilt; bandits everywhere seized the moment and rose like hedgehog quills standing on end.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Emperor Yang lost the Mandate; Heaven recoiled from his deeds; the people paid the price; rebels rose on every side like bristling quills.

sentences.zh: 其劇者，若李密因黎陽，蕭銑始江陵，竇建德連河北，王世充舉東都，皆磨牙搖毒以相噬螫。

translations.literal: The most violent were such men as Li Mi, who relied on Liyang; Xiao Xian, who began at Jiangling; Dou Jiande, who linked Hebei; and Wang Shichong, who raised the Eastern Capital — all gnashing their teeth and shaking poison to bite and sting one another.
translations.idiomatic: The fiercest were Li Mi at Liyang, Xiao Xian at Jiangling, Dou Jiande across Hebei, and Wang Shichong at the Eastern Capital — each gnashing his teeth and trading venom in mutual destruction.

sentences.zh: 其間亦假仁義，禮賢才，因之擅王僭帝，所謂盜亦有道者。

translations.literal: Among them some also borrowed benevolence and righteousness, honored worthy talent, and thereby usurped kingship and emperorship — what is called "even thieves have their way."
translations.idiomatic: Even among them some feigned benevolence, honored men of talent, and on that basis seized royal or imperial titles — as the saying goes, even thieves have their code.

sentences.zh: 本夫孽氣腥焰，所以亡隋，觸唐明德，折北不支，禍極兇殫，乃就殲夷，宜哉！

translations.literal: In origin it was the baleful vapor and bloody flame that destroyed Sui; when they collided with Tang's bright virtue they broke northward and could not hold; when calamity reached its limit and villainy was exhausted, they were at last wiped out — as was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the reeking, blood-soaked tide that brought down the Sui. When it met Tang's bright virtue it shattered and could not stand. Calamity ran its course, villainy was spent, and they were destroyed — as was only fitting!
